subject: fix(ally-be): send the product-updates digest only from the production database
title: send the product-updates digest only from the production database
body:
Env files get copied between environments. A non-prod environment that kept
PRODUCT_UPDATES_ENABLED and PRODUCT_UPDATES_DIGEST_TO sent its own digest at
18:30 IST on 2026-11-05, in the pre-redesign format, to the same recipients as
prod. Its Redis lock is separate, so nothing stopped it.

The digest now requires DB_DATABASE to end in _prd (prod is ally_prd). Elsewhere
sendIfDue returns 'not-production' before taking the lock or calling SES, and
logs one warning a day so the skip is visible.

Verified: jest src/product-updates src/config (101 pass), eslint and tsc clean.

subject: fix(scribe-review): add auth guard to unread-count endpoint
title: add auth guard to unread-count endpoint
body:
The /api/v1/scribe-session-reviews/unread-count endpoint was throwing a TypeError because it was not properly guarded for authentication, and was trying to access req.user.id when req.user was undefined.

This commit adds the JwtAuthGuard to the endpoint to ensure that a user is authenticated before accessing the endpoint. The manual permission check is replaced with the @AuthPermissions decorator for consistency.

subject: fix(character-interview): unquote language keys and reject ones that resolve to nothing
title: unquote language keys and reject ones that resolve to nothing
body:
A production interview draft arrived with its per-language maps keyed
"'14'" — the model quoted the key itself — and the draft tool stored it
as-is. The character create endpoint accepts only numeric languageId
keys, so the trainer's save of the reviewed character failed with
400 "languageCharacteristics \"'14'\" is not a valid language id".

The language-key resolver now strips wrapping quotes (straight, smart
and backticks) before resolving, which files that draft correctly under
language 14. A key that still resolves to no language is no longer
passed through for the create endpoint to refuse at the trainer: the
draft is rejected with an instructive error so the agent re-keys and
retries, consistent with how every other draft defect is handled.

subject: fix(bug-hunter): keep coordinated plans moving instead of parking them
title: keep coordinated plans moving instead of parking them
body:
advancePlans only knew BLOCKED (next), MERGED (done) and a few stuck
statuses, so a plan with any other step status sat at "Fixing across repos"
forever with nothing running:
- a step already RELEASED/RELEASING never counted as merged, so the plan
  never finished;
- a step left NEW/APPROVED/PENDING_APPROVAL (its dispatch never happened)
  was neither in flight nor next;
- a REJECTED step neither halted the plan nor let it continue.

subject: fix(character-interview): require language style and dialect samples in the draft
title: require language style and dialect samples in the draft
body:
Characters created through the interview bot were arriving with their
Language style and Dialect samples sections empty: the interviewer prompt
asks for languageCharacteristics and linguisticStyleSamples, but both were
optional in the save_character_draft tool schema, so a model could skip
them with no error and the draft still saved.

Both fields are now in the schema's required list (models reliably satisfy
required fields), and a draft that still arrives with no style or no
samples is rejected with an instructive validation error — the agent fixes
the errors and retries, the path save_character_draft already uses for
every other limit. Presence only, not per-language completeness: the shape
leniency that files whatever a model sent stays as it is.

subject: fix(image-generation): move to gpt-image-1.5 and relax moderation for counselling topics
title: move to gpt-image-1.5 and relax moderation for counselling topics
body:
OpenAI retired gpt-image-1 on the Images API (and dall-e-3 entirely), which
broke every cover/course image generation. Two earlier fixes (#124, #134)
chased the wrong causes: coercing the model to the equally retired dall-e-3,
then blaming the default prompt's wording.

Verified against the live API:
- gpt-image-1.5 works at 1536x1024 / quality medium; the default and the
  retired names (gpt-image-1, dall-e-2, dall-e-3) from a stale env now
  resolve to it.
- A QPR (suicide-prevention) course description is refused under the default
  moderation but accepted under 'low', so the OpenAI provider now sends
  moderation: 'low' for gpt-image models — counselor-training covers
  legitimately name suicide, self-harm and abuse.
- "Try rewording it" is now shown only for genuine content refusals
  (moderation_blocked / content_policy_violation); any other 400 (retired
  model, invalid size) reports as an upstream failure instead of blaming the
  trainer's prompt, which is what sent the earlier fixes down the wrong road.

Also removes the ineffective 'documentary-style' prompt strip and updates the
three ai-task-registry image rows to the new default model.

subject: fix(badges): make-translations fills only missing languages
title: make-translations fills only missing languages
body:
The four XP_LEVEL ladder badges (Getting Going, Halfway Up, Seasoned, Top
of the Ladder) show in English in every app language. They were inserted
by migration 1950200000000-SeedXpLevelBadges with raw SQL, which skips
createBadge and so never translated them: translations is null.

POST /badges/make-translations could backfill them, but it re-translated
every badge into every language and replaced the whole translations
object, overwriting any translation a person had corrected.

It now asks for only the languages a badge is missing and merges them
into what is there. A language counts as missing when it has no entry, no
name, no description while the badge has one, or a name identical to the
English one: translateObjectToLanguages stores the English source as the
translation when a call fails, so an English copy is a past failure.

Checked: jest src/badge (85 tests, 4 new: seeded badge gets all four
languages; fully translated badge untouched; partial badge gets only the
gap with the rest kept; English copy re-translated), eslint, tsc.

body:
Follow-up to 29519b1da. `listPullRequestFiles` never throws: a GitHub error

targets, so `checkReleaseHealth` recorded "no health URL" as checked and the
release was never verified — one transient 5xx during the tick was enough.

On a truncated listing the row's service is used, as every release was
checked before the move; it may miss a second target, never the first.

subject: fix(builder-eval): never reuse a prompt-gate baseline from before a fixture edit (#5)
title: never reuse a prompt-gate baseline from before a fixture edit (#5)
body:
* fix(builder-eval): never reuse a prompt-gate baseline from before a fixture edit

A prompt gate reuses a completed suite on the same fixtures for up to 7 days,
matched by fixture id, loop and overrides. Nothing checked whether a fixture
had been edited since: PATCH /fixtures/:id and an import that matches by name
both change a fixture's checklist or admin script in place. A candidate could
then be scored on the new checklist and compared with a baseline scored on the
old one, and credited (or blamed) for the edit.

resolveBaseline now takes the candidate's fixtures, as it loaded them, and
reuses a suite only if it was created after every one of them was last
updated. Otherwise a fresh baseline runs alongside, as before. Both timestamps
are set by the database, so there is no clock skew between them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(builder-eval): log which fixture edit kept a baseline from being reused

A fresh baseline costs a full suite, and nothing on any page says why one
ran. When a suite would have been reused but for an edit, log the skipped
baseline (id, start) and the fixture whose edit ruled it out (name, id,
updatedAt).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(builder-eval): say on the gate's verdict when a fixture edit forced a fresh baseline

The log line alone meant reading CloudWatch to learn why a gate cost an extra
suite. resolveBaseline now returns a note with the baseline. When an edit
ruled out the latest comparable suite, execute appends it to verdict.reasons,
which the admin Suite panel already lists:
"Ran a fresh baseline: the latest one on these fixtures (<id>) started

subject: fix(i18n): ciSync repairs drafts that echo English over a real translation
title: ciSync repairs drafts that echo English over a real translation
body:
The hi/mr/ta/kn drafts held the literal English text for 43 keys
(review.filter.*, review.sort.*, profile.settings.appearance.*, ...)
while the repo bundles had carried real translations for months - the
Review tabs showed "Read"/"Unread" in every language. ciSync's presence
check counted that seeding debris as a translation, so additive-only
sync could never heal it.

Treat a draft value identical to the incoming English value as absent
when this language's repo bundle disagrees with English: English
squatting on a translated key is the same disease as the blanks fixed
after the 2026-10-01 incident. A deliberate English-looking translation
("OK") survives, since its repo value equals English too.

The helpline release workflow's i18n:publish step runs ci-sync, so the
next helpline release after this deploys repairs all drifted keys.

subject: fix(llm-agent): unique Gemini tool-call ids across passes; a refused call is not a failure
title: unique Gemini tool-call ids across passes; a refused call is not a failure
body:
Found in the W2b live check on gemini-2.5-pro: the draft saved, the model
tried save_character_draft again in the next pass (refused — only
finish_turn was left), and the reply went out with "an edit failed and
nothing repaired it" and the save listed twice under Failed.

Two causes:
- Gemini has no tool-call ids, so the adapter minted `gemini_<tool>_<index>`
  — unique within one response, repeated across the passes of one turn. Every
  per-turn join of calls to results by id read the later result for both.
  Ids now carry a per-response suffix. This also fixes Builder's W2a receipts
  on Gemini (its live model) for new turns.
- The runner counted a call it refused to run as a failed edit. It is now
  marked notRun and left out of the failure checks and the receipt.

The runtime's joinCallsToResults also joins by occurrence, so rows stored
with repeated ids still read right.

subject: fix(builder): an eval suite with no loop stamped replays the legacy loop
title: an eval suite with no loop stamped replays the legacy loop
body:
ally-be#689 stamps the interview loop on every new eval suite, but the sandbox
fell back to the LIVE validatedTurns setting for a suite with no stamp. Suites
started before v1.155.0 and resumed across its deploy (ally-be#684 resumes them)
therefore switched to validated turns halfway through — two prod baseline suites
(0e6299a3, 18b6fe96) were mid-run when it deployed, with dozens of runs queued.

An unstamped suite now always replays the legacy loop it started on, as the docs
already said, and the sandbox no longer reads live settings at all. Each run
records the loop it replayed in metrics.loop, so a suite's runs can be checked.

title: org-restricted admins can load and save their chart layout
body:

subject: fix(debrief-feedback): only the session's learner can rate its debrief
title: only the session's learner can rate its debrief
body:
POST /v1/scenario-sessions/:sessionId/debrief-feedback checked auth and
tenant but not who owns the session. Any user in the tenant could rate
another learner's debrief first: the one-row-per-session constraint then
409'd the learner, and the rating judged that session's skill-experiment
observation (score 100/0), steering the champion/challenger outcome.

The service now loads the session within the tenant (404 if absent) and
rejects anyone but its counselorId (403), before touching feedback or the
observation. The controller passes the caller's user id, 401s without
one, and validates the session id as a UUID so a malformed id is a 400
rather than a Postgres error.

subject: fix(chat): a cached chat no longer crosses orgs; hold summary export to scope
title: a cached chat no longer crosses orgs; hold summary export to scope
body:
ChatService.getChatById filters by the caller's JWT tenant, but returned
any cached chat by id first — and the cache key carries no tenant. Any
caller who could reach a chat id (a tenant ADMIN exporting a summary holds
ORGANIZATION_ACCESS) got another org's chat once that org had cached it.
A cache hit now has to pass the same tenant test as the query.

exportSummary also checks the chat's org against TenantScopeService, so a
platform admin restricted to some orgs — whose token carries no tenant and
so matches every chat — is held to them. Out of scope answers 404, not 403:
chat ids are sequential.

subject: fix(llm): send a system-only Gemini prompt as a user turn
title: send a system-only Gemini prompt as a user turn
body:
Gemini rejects a call with no contents ("contents are required"), and the
provider moves every system message into systemInstruction. A prompt made only
of system messages therefore failed on every request. Since 4d73f058 moved
course translation to Gemini, the keyed-translation call (system message only)
failed for every field of every course: all 12 fields of a fresh course in
production, titles and descriptions included.

When there are no user/assistant turns, send the system text as the single
user turn instead. Mixed conversations are unchanged.

The existing spec mocks the SDK, so it never saw the SDK's own contents check;
the new tests reproduce that rule and fail on the old code.

subject: fix(track): org-restricted admins edit only their own courses, never global
title: org-restricted admins edit only their own courses, never global
body:
Tracks are global content, served to every org they are assigned to, and
nothing checked who created one — unlike roleplays, where an allowlisted
admin may change only their own. A platform admin restricted to some orgs
could edit, delete, duplicate or re-translate any course, and set isGlobal,
which assigns a course to every org at once.

TrackService.assertCallerMayEdit / assertCallerMayMakeGlobal apply the
roleplay rule; the admin controller runs them ahead of the 11 routes that
change an existing course and on create/update. Reading the library and
assigning courses to their own orgs is unchanged.

subject: fix(builder): a fix that never reached the branch is not a fix
title: a fix that never reached the branch is not a fix
body:
On ally-mobile#114 opencode switched branches while fixing review
findings; opencode github then skipped the push ("Agent managed its own
branch"), the work was lost, and its reply still said every item was
fixed. Builder read "finished, branch unmoved" as opencode disagreeing

bugs.

  standing rules: stay on the current branch; don't create or switch
  branches, commit or push; say so if nothing changed.

  decide when to stop, not the reply.

subject: fix(builder): label the issue for real, and hand the spec to opencode by file
title: label the issue for real, and hand the spec to opencode by file
body:
Two things the first production issue build (ally-be#629) hit:

- GitHub drops labels on a new issue, without an error, when the token can
  open issues but not label them, so the issue's workflow never started.
  Builder now checks the label stuck, adds it once more if not, and otherwise
  fails the build naming the permission the token needs.
- The workflow passed the prompt through GITHUB_ENV with a heredoc delimiter;
  the spec has no trailing newline, so the delimiter landed mid-line and the
  step failed. The prompt now goes to a file that the opencode step reads,
  which also avoids env size limits on a large design.

subject: fix(scenario-report): cancel the ai-learn run when ally-be gives up on a report
title: cancel the ai-learn run when ally-be gives up on a report
body:
ally-be marks a studio rehearsal report FAILED after 30 minutes (Redis key
expiry handler and the stale-report cron) or when its trigger fails, but only
a user's Cancel ever told ai-learn to stop. The simulated turns and the
evaluator kept running for a report nobody would see.

- handleExpiredReportGeneration, markStaleReportsAsFailed and the trigger
  failure path now send the same cancel request (ENDPOINTS.SCENARIO_REPORT_CANCEL)
  after the report is marked FAILED. Best-effort: a cancel failure is logged
  and never blocks or undoes the FAILED write. The expiry path sends it only
  from the replica that won the conditional update; the trigger path only if
  the generate request was actually attempted (its RetryOnFail can fail after
  an earlier attempt reached ai-learn).
- triggerScenarioReportCancel gets an explicit 10s timeout instead of the
  5-minute makeRequest default, since the cron tick now waits on it.
- Documented on triggerScenarioReportGenerate that a retry can resend a
  report_id ai-learn is already running, and that any 2xx (ai-learn's answer
  to a duplicate) is treated as started.

subject: fix(builder): make gate rechecks cheap, and make ally-web's test check real
title: make gate rechecks cheap, and make ally-web's test check real
body:
Run 2 of session 178e6598 spent ~6 minutes per gate round on ally-web's
`nx affected -t test`, which runs every spec in each touched project (5,631
admin + 3,170 helpline tests for a two-file change), across four rounds.
It also couldn't fail a build: vitest wraps FAIL in ANSI colour codes, so
the parser named nothing on either side, and "red on master, red now,
nothing parsed" read as no new failures. Replayed on that run's logs, the
fixed parser finds 15 new failures the gate let through (the agent's own
CompletionRuleFields.test.tsx and 7 TrackOverview cases); 62 failures that
were already red on master are carried over.

- parse-check-failures: strip ANSI first; name vitest failures by their
  full `|project| file > case` line; drop vitest's bare "70ms" durations;
  read nx's `::group::❌ > nx run` header used on runners.
- ally-web affectedTest: `vitest related --run` on the files changed
  against origin/master (96 spec files, <20s locally for run 2's change);
  `test` (the baseline) moves to root `vitest run` so both sides print the
  same failure names. Needs an ally-be release, since the gate reads the
  command table from the API.
- run-test-gate: reuse a repo's results from an earlier round in the same
  job when its working tree hashes identically, so a round that only
  touched ally-be doesn't re-run ally-web.

subject: fix(rate-limit): trust the load balancer's X-Forwarded-For so req.ip is the client
title: trust the load balancer's X-Forwarded-For so req.ip is the client
body:
ally-be never set Express's `trust proxy`, so behind the load balancer in
front of every deployment, req.ip was the balancer's own address. Every
IP-keyed rate limit (magic-link verify, the AI Lab evaluator login) counted
all clients as one, and both audit loggers recorded the balancer instead of
the caller.

main.ts now sets `trust proxy` to TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS = 1. The API hostname
resolves straight to an AWS Application Load Balancer, and the ECS task runs
Node with nothing in front of it, in dev and production alike. One hop makes
req.ip the address the balancer appended to X-Forwarded-For, and ignores
anything a client wrote into the header itself. It is deliberately a hop
count and never `true`, which would let any caller pick its own req.ip.

CustomThrottlerGuard now reads req.ip alone. `req.ips?.[0] || req.ip` gave
the same value under any setting, but read as trusting the header. Nothing
reads req.protocol, req.hostname or req.secure, the other values the setting
changes. DATA_SCHEMA.md now notes that audit_logs.ip_address rows from before
this change hold the balancer's address.

network.constants.spec.ts pins what req.ip resolves to, including a spoofed
left-most entry and the unset setting production ran with. The route spec
now mirrors main.ts and shows two clients get separate otp buckets while a
spoofed address gets no fresh one; that test fails without the setting.

subject: fix(character-interview): stop the wrap-up pass announcing an unsaved draft
title: stop the wrap-up pass announcing an unsaved draft
body:
A helpline admin was told "I've compiled everything ... it's now ready
for your final review", but no review form opened and the session never
completed. That sign-off is what the prompt asks for after
save_character_draft succeeds. It can also come from the tool-less
wrap-up pass a turn makes once it hits the 8 round-trip cap. On that
pass the model cannot call the tool and was never told that nothing had
been saved.

- When no draft was saved this turn, the wrap-up pass's system prompt
  now says so and forbids implying the character is ready. It goes in
  the system prompt, not a trailing message, so the tool results are not
  followed by a second user turn in a row.
- If the turn tried save_character_draft and never succeeded, the turn
  is marked failed (`draft_not_saved`) with copy asking the admin to
  reply "try again", so the admin is not relying on the model to say it.
  The row persists as errored, so a reload still shows it. A truncated
  wrap-up keeps its own, earlier error.
- The AI task registry row now records the extra wrap-up call.

Not confirmed against the production transcript: prod log access was
down when this was written. The line to look for is "hit the
8-iteration cap".

subject: fix(builder): a failed review no longer strands its pull request
title: a failed review no longer strands its pull request
body:
`dispatchReviewRun` stamps `reviewedSha` before dispatching, which is correct
and load-bearing: reconcile runs every five minutes and would otherwise send a
second reviewer at a pull request the first is still reading.

But the stamp means "a review was attempted at this commit" and
`considerReviewRun` reads it as "this commit has been reviewed". For a run that
finished those are the same thing; for one that failed they are not, and
nothing told them apart. So a single failure stranded the pull request for
good: its head never moves again on its own, `reviewedSha === headSha` holds
forever, no second review is dispatched, `reviewPassedSha` is never written,
and approval and auto-merge both wait on evidence that can no longer arrive.

ally-be#503 has been in that state since 2026-09-17; migration 1971200000000
records ally-be#494 doing the same before it. Neither is touched here — this
stops the next one.

`reviewRunCount` is deliberately not refunded. It is what bounds the retry: a
pull request still gets at most BUILDER_MAX_REVIEW_RUNS_PER_PR dispatches, so
an engine failing every time costs two runs rather than an endless supply.
Clearing the sha buys a retry, not a loop.

Also merges builder_coder_guidance. The dashboard version and the file had
diverged into two different sets of advice — the file carrying Ally's traps
(guarded paths, never edit a merged migration), the dashboard carrying general
discipline (never invent a requirement, match the code around you) — and
turning on dashboard override would have made whichever one lost the silent
winner. Both are kept.

title: a mined pair is confirmed only if counsellors say it
body:
The evidence rule confirms when counsellors say the replacement OR the
agent says the avoid-term. Every mined candidate is a word the agent
says, so on the v1.141.3 prod dry runs every uncontradicted pair read

counsellor had ever said. For mined pairs, "confirmed" now requires

subject: fix(github): a rollup that cannot be read is not a commit without checks
title: a rollup that cannot be read is not a commit without checks
body:
Both halves of getCheckRollup swallowed their error into an empty list, so a
403 or 404 — a token without Checks permission on one repo, a rate limit, a
timeout — produced total = 0 and a confident `state: 'none'`.

That is not a near-miss. It is a commit with four green checks reported as a
commit nobody verified, and every gate that waits for green then waits
forever: considerReviewRun stands down, approval never comes, auto-merge
declines, and the merge button tells a person "this pull request has no checks
at all", which is the one sentence guaranteed to send them looking at CI
instead of at the token.

ally-mobile#104 has been in that state all day. GitHub reports four successful
check-runs on its head; the reconcile row, written three minutes before this
was found, said ciStatus "none". Reconcile was running the whole time and
faithfully recording an answer that was never true.

Null is what the callers already expect from an unanswered question: reconcile
keeps the last known status rather than overwriting it with a guess, and
mergePullRequest refuses to merge blind. The failure is now loud where it used
to be indistinguishable from good news.

subject: fix(builder): make "mark all as read" actually mark anything as read
title: make "mark all as read" actually mark anything as read
body:
The criteria said `readAt: null`, which TypeORM renders as `WHERE "readAt" =
NULL`. That is never true of any row, so the update matched nothing — and the
endpoint above it answered `{ ok: true }` for work it had not done. The bell
sat on fifty unread, "mark all read" did nothing visible, and the response said
everything was fine. A success reported for work that did not happen is the
failure mode nobody thinks to investigate.

The `as any` the old criteria needed was the tell: the types objected before
the database did. Every read path in this service already used `IsNull()`, and
so does Bug Hunter's equivalent repository. This was the one that did not.

Worth recording how it survived a fix: ally-web#713 was raised against exactly
this symptom, but its session was scoped to ally-web alone, so the only layer
it could edit was the client. It added a refetch and tag invalidation, and a
test asserting the query is invalidated after the mutation — all of which was
already true and is still true. The gate passed on a change that could not have
worked. The tests here assert the criteria itself rather than that an update
was called, because the weaker assertion passes against the broken version.

subject: fix(builder): a plan is not an outcome
title: a plan is not an outcome
body:
Build 36049077956 dispatched at 19:34, and at 19:38 its PLANNING agent finished
writing the plan and called `complete_run done`. ally-be accepted it: a planner
edits no files, so the `changedNothing` exemption waved the gate requirement
through and the run was settled before the coder had started. The pipeline
carried on regardless, coded, hit failing tests, and the reconcile tick logged
"reported done and then failed; correcting session" eight minutes later.
Thirty-four minutes, no pull request.

`changedNothing` exists for fix runs that correctly find nothing to act on, and
that exemption stays — two such runs were once recorded FAILED for doing the
right thing. What it cannot be allowed to mean is "the run is over", because a
planner has by definition touched nothing and is by definition not finished.

So the stage decides. A run may not report `done` while the rail still reads
SETUP or PLANNING, whatever the agent believes and whatever the file check
would have excused. Failures from those stages still record: the runner reports
those from evidence after the agent has gone, and losing one strands the run.

The rule deliberately applies to EVERY mode. My first cut scoped it to BUILD,
and a failing test — a mocked run with no `mode` — made the better rule
obvious: a fix run skips the planner and reports from CODING, a review reports
from REVIEWING, and there is no mode whose work is finished while the rail
reads PLANNING. No exceptions needed, and it holds for a run whose mode is
missing entirely.

## Why this surfaced now

It was always reachable — the shared prompt header has always documented
`complete-run` to every phase. But it was a shell command an agent had to
compose, and it is now a typed tool sitting in every phase's tool list, because
I moved the reporting protocol to MCP yesterday. Making a protocol easier to
call correctly makes it easier to call wrongly, and the guard for that belongs
on the server rather than in a phase prompt. Same lesson as "asked for, or made
true", arriving from the other direction.

The same run is also the first production proof the MCP server works:
`mcp_builder_complete_run` returned "Outcome recorded." and `mcp_builder_todo`
returned "checklist updated" — which incidentally fixes the checklist that had
been stuck at 0 of 7, since the agent now updates it mid-run.

Verified: builder suite 555/555, tsc and eslint clean.

subject: fix(ai): redact sensitive data in error logs
title: redact sensitive data in error logs
body:
When a request to the AI service fails, the error logger writes the full request body to the logs, even when the redactBody flag is true. This could expose sensitive user data in the logs, such as personal information or health-related data, which should be protected.

This commit fixes the issue by checking the redactBody flag in the error handling block of the makeRequest method in AiService. If the flag is true, the request body is redacted in the error logs.

A regression test has been added to ensure that the request body is redacted in error logs when the redactBody flag is true.

subject: fix(cloud-telephony): remove redundant disconnect handler
title: remove redundant disconnect handler
body:
Removes a redundant event handler for the 'disconnect' event in the CloudTelephonyGateway.
The OnGatewayDisconnect lifecycle hook already handles teardown logic for a disconnecting client.
The manual listener was causing the 'handleDisconnect' method to be called twice, leading to 'Session not found for client' errors when the second call could not find the session that the first call had already cleaned up.

A regression test has been added to ensure that the 'disconnect' event listener does not manually call 'handleDisconnect', preventing this issue from recurring.

subject: fix(scheduler): Handle undefined userId in scheduled tasks
title: Handle undefined userId in scheduled tasks
body:
The scheduled task `ios-min-version-auto-bump` was failing in production with the error `invalid input syntax for type integer: "NaN"`. This was caused by the `ExecutionManager.getUserId()` returning `undefined` in a scheduled task context, which was then converted to `NaN` when passed to `Number()`.

This commit fixes the issue by providing a default value of `0` when `ExecutionManager.getUserId()` returns a falsy value. This is consistent with other parts of the codebase where a system user is represented by the ID `0`.

A regression test has been added to ensure that `updatedBy` is set to `0` when a user is not present in the execution context.

subject: fix(builder): a run's own account of itself is no longer lost to its newlines
title: a run's own account of itself is no longer lost to its newlines
body:
The run that shipped ally-web#694 this morning planned, coded, remediated,
passed its gate, passed an independent review and opened a pull request — and
its write-up never reached ally-be:

    POST /pipeline/runs/c39ca460…/report
      → BadRequestException: Unexpected token '#', "## What…

The agent had done nothing wrong. It wrote the documented envelope:

    cat > /tmp/report.json <<'EOF'
    { "type": "run_report", "contentMd": "## What was done
    …

A JSON string cannot hold a literal newline, and a run report is nothing but
newlines. So the one payload in the reporting protocol that still asked a model
to hand-assemble JSON around multi-line prose produced invalid JSON, ally-be
answered 400, and `report` swallowed it — every helper ends in `|| true`,
because telemetry must never fail a build. The E2E decision, the docs-guard
result and a reviewer's note about missing aria labels in en.ts were all
composed and then thrown away, and nothing anywhere said so.

This is the same problem the pull request body already solved and for the same
reason: the agent writes plain markdown to a file and the RUNNER composes. That
path has never failed. `report` now works the same way — hand it prose, and the
escaping is jq's problem rather than a model's. A well-formed envelope is still
passed through untouched, so a caller that gets it right is unaffected, and a
body that is neither is treated as the markdown it plainly is, which is what
recovers this morning's failure rather than merely refusing it more clearly.

And when the POST is refused anyway, it is now SAID — in the run feed, the only
surface a person actually reads. A dropped report was invisible by
construction: the helper may not fail the build and the runner's stdout has no
consumers, so a 400 here had no reader at all. It still cannot fail the build.

`report-helper.test.mjs` runs the helper as a real subprocess against a server
that parses bodies the way Nest does, and pins this morning's exact body as a
regression. Wired into test.yml beside the other runner harnesses, which is
where it would have been caught.

Verified: report helper 4/4 including the captured failing body; loop-dryrun
91/91; builder constants 68/68.

subject: fix(learn): Give the roleplay log filter a way to tell same-named people apart
title: Give the roleplay log filter a way to tell same-named people apart
body:
Display names are not unique within a tenant. Production has three separate
accounts named "Sandeep Malhotra", two "Shubham Bhoite" and two "Tanuja Babre"
— seven accounts across three names, in one tenant.

This was found by filtering prod: picking "Shubham Bhoite" returned a single
session, which looked broken. It was not. That option was id 99, which really
does have one session; the other Shubham is id 123, with 328. Selecting both
returns exactly 329, so the filter was already correct — it is the picker that
could not express which person was meant.

Filtering by id rather than name is what makes this a labelling problem instead
of a correctness one: a name-based filter would have silently merged the three
Sandeeps into one result set, which is precisely the wrong answer for an admin
reviewing one person's practice.

admin-scenario-session-filters now returns each person's email so the client
has something to disambiguate by. It shows the email only for names that
actually repeat, leaving the other thirty options unchanged.

subject: fix(i18n): contract placeholders to the source language, not a cell's own past (#508)
title: contract placeholders to the source language, not a cell's own past (#508)
body:
`validatePlaceholders` compared a new value against that same cell's previous
value, so a `{{variable}}` could never be removed from a published key by any
route: the dashboard rejected the edit, and `ciSync` only ever adds keys it has
not seen. Copy that dropped a variable the code had stopped interpolating could
not reach production at all.

That is not a hypothetical. `00fc8372` (ally-web) stopped passing `max` to
`postSim.debrief.replyPlaceholder` and rewrote the copy in all five locale
files, but the published bundle still carries the old string — so the debrief
composer on app.helloally.ai renders a literal `(0/{{max}})`.

English owns the contract instead, matching what the Add key flow already does:

- editing `en` is never blocked — introducing or retiring a placeholder is a
  code decision, and English is where it lands;
- every other language is validated against the current English draft.

Auto-translate is held to the same contract: a model that drops `{{name}}`
from its output now falls back to the source value and is reported in `failed`,
rather than writing a broken translation straight past the guard.

Docs pick up the placeholder contract and, separately, the repo-vs-published
trap that made this invisible: once a key is published, editing the repo locale
file changes nothing, because the published bundle is layered over the shipped
one at runtime.

title: the course progress dashboard shows the learner's roleplay score
body:
SS-4172-2026-09-16 read 60 in Roleplay Logs and 78 on the course progress
dashboard. Both numbers were real; they were different measures of the same
session, and only one of them belongs to the learner.

`scenario_sessions.score` is the learner-facing roleplay score: the -100..100

attempt judged at all?" test for the skillCoverage and markdown feedback this

subject: fix(builder): a premature completion is refused, not fatal, and the agent is told
title: a premature completion is refused, not fatal, and the agent is told
body:
A fresh Gemini build called `complete-run done` in the middle of the coding
phase, before the gate it was claiming had run at all. Two things then went
wrong, and both of them are ours.

The claim ended the run. `/complete` settled FAILED on a `done` with no passing
gate, on the assumption that such a claim came from an agent about to exit. It
also arrives from one that completed too early — and that run carried on
through the gate, remediation and finalise behind a session already painted
red by a claim the pipeline had itself overtaken. It is refused now, with 409,
and the run is left alone: an agent that does go on to quit is caught by
outcome-gate.sh, which settles whatever is still RUNNING when the engine exits.
The verdict comes from what happened rather than from what was claimed halfway
through.

The agent was told it had succeeded. The refusal came back as HTTP 200 with
`{"ok": false}` and the helper checked only the status code, so it printed
"Outcome recorded." at an agent whose outcome had just been rejected. It
believed it had finished, said so, and stopped. `complete-run` now reads the
body as well as the code, treats a 4xx as final rather than retrying a
considered answer three times, and prints the server's reason.

subject: fix(builder): the default-engine picker applies to new sessions
title: the default-engine picker applies to new sessions
body:
`builder_sessions.engine` carries a column default of 'claude-code', so
`session.engine` is never null — and the dispatch reads
`overrides.engine ?? session.engine ?? settings.defaultEngine`, where a
non-null column default makes the third rung unreachable. The admin's default
engine therefore applied to no new session ever: every one arrived at dispatch
already saying claude-code. An earlier fix added that fallback and could not
have worked.

Worse than doing nothing, because the per-tier MODELS do read settings. A
workspace set to Gemini produced a claude-code engine with `gemini-2.5-pro` as
its coder: the first fresh session of the day planned on claude-haiku-4-5 —
correct for a Claude engine — and then died on its first coding invocation,
having spent $0.28 discovering that.

Stamped at creation, where the identical bug in `defaultBudgetUsd` was fixed
three lines above: documented as applied to a new session, never read, every
session uncapped. The session now records the engine it will actually run on,
which is also what the UI reads back.

Not made nullable instead: the column default is load-bearing for existing
rows, and a session recording its engine is the behaviour the rest of the code
already assumes.

subject: fix(builder): a completed session that shipped nothing is not a dead end
title: a completed session that shipped nothing is not a dead end
body:
`getDeliveryState` already states the rule — "a session with no pull requests
has shipped nothing, whatever its status" — and startability did not apply it.
COMPLETED was refused outright, which is right for a session whose pull
requests are open or merged and wrong for one whose branch is empty.

That state is reachable and was reached: a run whose agent claimed done and
whose evidence said otherwise settles the session green with nothing behind it.
Combined with COMPLETED being unrestartable, the page offered no way onward
from a success that did not happen — the same dead end as stopping a build,
one status along.

A completed session WITH pull requests still refuses: a second build against
the same PRD opens a competing set.

subject: fix(builder): evidence can correct a success the agent claimed
title: evidence can correct a success the agent claimed
body:
Run 4 ended with the session green and nothing shipped. The agent called
`complete-run done`, which settled the run SUCCEEDED and the session COMPLETED.
Seconds later the runner found the truth — work pushed, no pull request — and
called `complete-run failed`. That updated the run row and stopped there:
`settleRun` returns early unless the session is BUILDING or WAITING_FOR_INPUT,
and the agent's own claim had already moved it past both.

The result is the worst shape this can take. The session reads Done in green,
its own latest run reads Failed, no pull request exists, and COMPLETED is
deliberately not restartable — so the page offers no way onward from a success
that did not happen.

The guard is right in general: a session a person cancelled must not be
overruled by a run finishing a moment later. It is wrong for a run correcting
itself, which is exactly the case the runner's evidence-based reports create —
they always arrive after the agent's.

Narrowed rather than removed: only a FAILED settlement, only from the session's
own latest run, only over a COMPLETED. Evidence may correct a claim; a claim
may not overwrite evidence, and no older run can reopen a session that has
moved on. Four cases cover it, including the two that must NOT move — a
cancelled session, and a SUCCEEDED settlement over a FAILED one.

subject: fix(builder): a stopped session can start another build
title: a stopped session can start another build
body:
`startBuild` accepted PRD_READY and FAILED only, so pressing stop was a
one-way door: the PRD stayed, the branch stayed, and every attempt to build
again was refused with "A build can only start from a ready PRD — this session
is cancelled." The only route onward was a new session and a re-run of the
interview.

A session reaches CANCELLED only by way of BUILDING, so its PRD is ready by
construction. Stopping a run says "not this build", not "retire this work".

COMPLETED stays out: its pull requests are open or merged, and a second build
against the same PRD opens a competing set.

The list is named and exported because the admin UI makes the same decision
about which sessions offer a start control, and the two had already drifted —
ally-web 9b54276e added the button for CANCELLED and the API refused it, so the
control was there and always errored. Found by clicking it.

Docs-Skip: no documented behaviour changes shape; the Builder page describes
statuses, not which ones dispatch

subject: fix(release): read past the first page of tags when picking a version
title: read past the first page of tags when picking a version
body:
`nextPatchTag` asked GitHub for one page of tags and treated it as the repo.
ally-web carries three independently-released apps, so its tags interleave three
prefixes — and its first 100 are ALL `helpline-v*`. The `admin-v*` scan
therefore matched nothing, fell into the "never released" branch, and proposed
`admin-v0.0.1` for an app on 1.88.

That is what Builder's auto-release did to ally-web#658: dispatched
`admin-v0.0.1`, and the release workflow's version validation rejected it. The
pull request is recorded `releaseState: failed` — merged but not deployed —
which is the state this whole feature exists to surface, so the reporting was
right even though the version was nonsense. The validation refusing it is the
only reason this was a failed release rather than a catastrophic one.

Now paged, to a bound, in the same shape as `listPullRequestFiles`.

The more important half is the empty case. "No tag carries this prefix" and "I
did not look far enough" produce an identical empty list and mean opposite
things, and they were sharing an answer — the most dangerous one available,
since proposing a first release for something already at 1.88 is a version
number that walks backwards. They are now separated on evidence: only a short
final page proves every tag was seen, and that alone earns `0.0.1`. Hitting the
page bound with tags still unread throws instead, because there is no safe guess
to make there.

Found while checking whether the roadmap sweep could mark an opportunity
shipped — it correctly refused, on a `failed` release nobody had looked at.

Docs-Skip: internal release helper, no API or schema surface change

subject: fix(builder): repair the type errors blocking every release
title: repair the type errors blocking every release
body:
`npm run build` has been failing on master since #497. Three errors, all from
that pull request and its follow-up #499:

- `builder-build.service.ts` uses `RecordBuilderRunModelDto` without importing
  it;
- `builder-pipeline.controller.spec.ts` calls `getRunOrFail` on a
  `Partial<BuilderBuildService>`, where every member is optional to the type
  checker even though `beforeEach` always provides it.

Nothing could be released while this stood: the Docker image runs `npm run
build`, so the build job failed and migration, deploy and the release draft were
all skipped. v1.125.0 died there, and so would anything else.

Worth noting how it got in. The pull request checks are green — Jest passes,
because ts-jest does not type-check the whole programme the way `nest build`
does, and nothing in the PR pipeline runs a real build. So a type error that
stops every deploy is invisible until someone cuts a release, which is the same
gap that took out v1.114.0. That is a CI problem rather than a code one, and it
deserves its own fix: a build step on the pull request, catching this where it
was written rather than an hour later in a release nobody expected to fail.

Docs-Skip: type-only repair, no API or schema surface change

subject: fix(builder): sweep sessions, not open pull requests
title: sweep sessions, not open pull requests
body:
The outcome reconciliation was written inside `reconcileOne`, which runs once
per pull request returned by `listReconcilable` — and that query filters on
`merged: false`. So for a session whose pull requests have all merged, the loop
iterates nothing and the reconciliation never runs.

Which is the one case it exists for. A merge is the strongest evidence a
session succeeded, and it is also exactly what removes a pull request from the
open set: the better the evidence got, the less reachable the code that reads
it became. Session 34d68cd2 sat at FAILED / E2E_VERIFY through two releases of
"fixes" for this, above two pull requests that had merged and deployed, because
the correction was on a code path that could no longer execute.

So it runs over sessions now — the recently-failed ones, bounded, newest first
— and asks each whether its verdict still matches what its pull requests did.

Deliberately before the GitHub guard, because the sweep is pure database work
and needs no credential. A dead token cost an entire afternoon of silent
no-ops today; there is no reason for this pass to share that fate. Each session
is caught individually so one bad row cannot stop the rest.

This is the third attempt at the same fix, and the previous two were wrong in
the same direction: both put the reconciliation somewhere that only sees open
pull requests. Found by watching the session instead of trusting the release.

subject: fix(builder): a merged pull request is the strongest evidence there is
title: a merged pull request is the strongest evidence there is
body:
The first cut of this scoped the evidence to OPEN pull requests and returned
early when there were none, on the reasoning that a session with nothing open
has "no evidence either way" and its last error is the only account of what
happened.

That is exactly backwards for a merge. A merged pull request carries green
checks AND a person explicitly choosing to take the change — there is no
stronger signal available anywhere in this system. Scoping it out meant a
session whose work had all shipped stayed FAILED for ever, which is the state
session 34d68cd2 ended in: both pull requests merged into master, both deployed,
and the page still saying the build failed with a phase rail frozen at
E2E_VERIFY.

Found by watching the session rather than trusting the fix, which is the only
reason it is not in production.

Closed WITHOUT merging keeps the old treatment, and that is the case the
original reasoning was really about: the work was looked at and turned down, so
whatever the session says about itself stands. Only the still-open pull requests
have anything left to prove, so they are what the CI and feedback checks
examine; a session whose pull requests have all merged passes on the merges
alone.

This changes a test that asserted the old behaviour. It was not wrong about what
the code did — it was wrong about what the code should do, and it is replaced by
one asserting the corrected rule rather than deleted.

subject: fix(builder): tell every run that CI happens after it, not during it
title: tell every run that CI happens after it, not during it
body:
Run 9 of session 34d68cd2 fixed a migration collision, pushed it, and went
green — then tried to WAIT for CI to confirm. It slept, echoed, and reached for
a scheduling tool; the sandbox refused each one in turn ("This command requires
approval", "`prompt` is required when `stop` is not true"). After 16 of its 24
turns and roughly $3.50 spent idling, it gave up and ended its turn without
calling `complete`.

`claude -p` exits 0 on `end_turn`, so the runner cannot tell that apart from
success. The outcome gate caught it and recorded a failure — correctly, and on
a run whose work was already merged-ready. The banner then advised retrying
work that was finished, and the run counted toward the circuit breaker.

The agent was not confused about the code. It was confused about where its job
ends. So the rule goes in the shared header rather than one prompt: every role
can push, and every role can be tempted to stay and watch.

It states the consequence rather than only the instruction. "Do not wait" is
advice; "ending your turn without calling `complete` is recorded as a run
failure even when your work pushed cleanly, and it counts toward the circuit
breaker" is the actual cost, and the one that should change the decision. It
also names where a red CI really gets handled — the reconcile loop's fix run,
which can read the failure the agent would only have been guessing at.

subject: fix(builder): let an answer whose resume failed be retried
title: let an answer whose resume failed be retried
body:
`answer()` writes the answer, then dispatches the resume. It has to be that
order — the resume reads the answer — but the two are not in one transaction, so
anything that throws in between leaves the question ANSWERED and the run still
WAITING_FOR_INPUT.

The budget ceiling throws in exactly that gap: `resumeFromQuestions` asserts it
AFTER the write. So answering an over-budget session consumed the question and
stranded the run, and re-answering refused it as a duplicate. That is not a
cosmetic dead end. A parked run counts as an ACTIVE run, and `dispatchFixRun`
and `dispatchReviewRun` both refuse to race one — silently, with no log and no
notification. From then on every fix and review dispatch for that session was
refused, and the only documented way out of WAITING_FOR_INPUT no longer existed.

I wedged ally-be#494's session this way: an answer attempt at 13:37 hit the
budget error, the question was consumed on the way, and nothing since could
dispatch.

So an answered question whose run is still parked is treated as a half-finished
answer rather than a duplicate one, and the half that failed is retried.
`resumeFromQuestions` re-checks group completeness and the budget and is safe to
call again; the answer itself is NOT rewritten, because it was recorded the
first time and overwriting it would discard what the person actually said. A
genuine duplicate — one whose run has since moved on — still refuses.

subject: fix(builder): drop a session error the pull requests have disproved
title: drop a session error the pull requests have disproved
body:
`settleRun` writes a failed run's error onto the run AND onto the session, and
only a new dispatch clears the session copy. That is fine while runs keep
coming. It is not fine when they cannot: a session over budget, parked on an
unanswered question, or blocked on a dead credential has no next dispatch, so
the banner stays up forever.

Which would be merely untidy if the text were vague. It is not. The gate error
reads "nothing proves the change works", and it has been sitting above two pull
requests whose every required check is green — the page stating the opposite of
the evidence, and pointing at the wrong thing to go and fix. It survived three
rounds of me explaining why it was still there instead of removing it.

So the claim is re-tested against the evidence on each reconcile rather than
left standing: every open pull request green, nothing actionable outstanding,
and the session's headline error has been overtaken by events.

Only the error, deliberately. The status is a separate question — a parked run
or a spent budget still means the session is not finished, and clearing that too
would trade one false statement for another.

Refuses in every case where the evidence does not support it: a red pull
request, one whose CI has not reported yet (unread is not passed), outstanding
actionable feedback, and a session with nothing open, whose last error is then
the only account of what happened.

subject: fix(builder): keeping a branch current is not a fix
title: keeping a branch current is not a fix
body:
`considerBranchUpdate` was gated on `autoFixEnabled`, which put two unrelated
things behind one switch: spending money on agent runs, and a single GitHub API
call that merges master into a branch. No agent, no model, no runner, no cost.

So the deliberate "review it, don't spend on it" setting — review on, fix off —
also switched off the free half. Both open Builder pull requests sat at
`behind`, which is not `clean`, which is exactly what `considerMergePrompt`
waits for before offering the merge button. Green, and in one case already
approved, and no way to finish: the loop went quiet with nothing to show and
nothing to click, which reads from the outside as the feature not working.

Now gated on the kill switch alone.

This drops a test asserting the old gate, whose stated reason was that agreeing
Builder may write code is not agreeing it may keep pushing to a branch somebody
is reviewing. That concern is real and it is still enforced — by a better guard
in the same method. `getCommitAuthor` plus `isOwnActor` means the branch is only
touched when Builder itself wrote the head commit, so nobody is mid-work on it.
`autoFixEnabled` was never what protected a human's branch; it only looked like
it did, at the cost of the merge button.

subject: fix(builder): doing the right thing must not look like failing
title: doing the right thing must not look like failing
body:
Two fix runs read their feedback, correctly found it was Builder's own approval
with nothing to act on, said so on the pull request and changed no code — and
were recorded FAILED. Not a faulty runner: the runner worked, the agent was
right, and `/complete` refused the `done` because no gate had run.

That rule is correct for a run that changed code, since "I fixed it" is not
checkable any other way. It is wrong for a run that makes no such claim. The
cost was not cosmetic: a healthy session showed Failed with a red banner, and
each of those failures counted toward the breaker that stops automatic work.

So a `done` from a run that edited nothing settles normally. `file_edit` is the
evidence and it is machine-emitted — the forwarder derives it from the engine's
output rather than taking the agent's word — so a run cannot claim it changed
nothing while having edited files. A run that DID edit files still needs its
gate, unchanged.

Also: a fix or review dispatch now clears the session error. Only a build
dispatch did, so a failure from three runs ago stayed on screen while newer runs
came and went — history rendered as current state.

subject: fix(builder): recognise its own pushes
title: recognise its own pushes
body:
`isOwnActor` matched `ally-builder*` and `*[bot]`. Every runner pushes as
`adminbughunterhelloallyai`, so Builder did not recognise its own commits — and
that one predicate decides two things, both of which failed silently:

  - a branch that fell behind master was never brought up to date, because the
    head commit looked like somebody else's work. That is why today's two pull
    requests sat BEHIND and the merge button could not appear: the prompt is
    gated on mergeable_state === 'clean', and BEHIND is not clean.
  - a failing check on Builder's own commit was filed OBSERVED instead of
    PENDING. `countPending` ignores OBSERVED, so the fix loop has never once
    fired on its own red CI. Yesterday's auto-fix worked only because a human's
    review comments triggered it.

The comment on `isOwnActor` describes this failure exactly — "a bot that
skipped its own comments but failed to recognise its own pushes would read a
branch it owns as somebody else's and stop fixing its own red CI". The reasoning
was right; the list just did not contain the name.

Now an explicit list of accounts, and an exact match rather than a prefix: a
person called `ally-builder-reviews` should not quietly gain the right to have
their pushes merged over.

Verified by mutation: removing the account name turns 2 of the 4 new tests red.

subject: fix(builder): announce a release that merged but never deployed
title: announce a release that merged but never deployed
body:
`RELEASE_FAILED` and `RELEASE_SKIPPED` were added with the release watcher and
never added to the announce list, so both wrote an in-app row and said nothing
anywhere a person looks. That quietly broke the promise auto-release was built
on: "merged but not deployed" reads as done from every angle — master has moved
on, the pull request is closed, CI is green — and the shout is the only thing
that makes it visible. A watcher whose verdict nobody sees is worse than no
watcher, because it looks like coverage.

RELEASE_FAILED is the strongest case in that list by its own stated rule.
RELEASE_SKIPPED is quieter and still belongs: a merged change waiting on a
manual release sits there until somebody notices, and it is at most one message
per merged pull request.

subject: fix: Production logs show multiple instances of an unhandled error during WebSocket authentication. This could lead to legiti (#491)
title: Production logs show multiple instances of an unhandled error during WebSocket authentication. This could lead to legiti (#491)
body:
This commit fixes a bug where unexpected errors during WebSocket
authentication were being caught and logged with a generic message,
obscuring the root cause of the failure.

The fix enhances the error handling in the WebSocketAuthMiddleware to
include the original error message in the UnauthorizedException that is
thrown. This ensures that more specific and actionable error information
is logged, which will aid in debugging and troubleshooting future
authentication issues.

A new regression test has been added to verify that unexpected errors
are now correctly propagated with their original error message. Existing
tests have been updated to align with this new behavior.

subject: fix(knowledge-base): includeArchived=false actually excludes archived documents
title: includeArchived=false actually excludes archived documents
body:
`@Type(() => Boolean)` on a query parameter is the obvious-looking choice and is
wrong: the value arrives as a STRING, and `Boolean("false")` is `true`. So
`?includeArchived=false` was read as true and archived documents were ALWAYS
returned.

Two consequences, both live in production until now:

  * The WhatsApp Corpus tab's "Show archived" checkbox has been inert in both
    positions since it shipped — unchecking it changed nothing.
  * Three documents archived in the character panel this afternoon kept
    rendering afterwards, which is what led me here.

Replaced with an explicit string comparison where only "true" is true, so an
absent parameter, an empty one, or a typo all mean "no" — the safe direction for
a flag whose job is to WIDEN a list. Real booleans still work, for JSON callers.
Six tests cover the string, boolean, casing and unrecognised cases.

The same `@Type(() => Boolean)` pattern is on `unreadOnly` in
src/bug-hunter/dto/bug-hunter.dto.ts and src/notification/dto/
notification-feed.dto.ts, where it means those feeds show only-unread when the
caller asked for everything. Left alone deliberately: fixing them changes what
two other features display, and their owners should see that rather than find it
in a diff of mine.

subject: fix(video-actor): walk the whole Beyond Presence roster
title: walk the whole Beyond Presence roster
body:
Their avatar list is paginated 10 to a page, reporting has_more with a
next_cursor, and this only ever read page one. So the Studio picker showed 10
of our 21 faces and an author had no way to know the rest existed — a
truncated roster is indistinguishable from a short one.

Among the hidden ones was bey's own default face, "Ege"
(b9be11b8-89fb-4227-8f86-4a881393cbdb), which renders perfectly well and is
exactly the id someone reading the plugin source would try to use. It also hid
the one avatar whose status is 'failed', so the availability filter was only
ever applied to the first page.

Now follows next_cursor until has_more is false, bounded by BEY_MAX_PAGES
rather than trusting a vendor to terminate a walk that runs inside a request
an author is waiting on. The bare-array shape bey has also returned from this
path is still accepted, and carries no cursor by definition.

Adds the service's first spec, pinning pagination specifically because this
class of bug is silent: it produces a shorter list, not an error. It also pins
two behaviours that were previously only comments — that a later page failing
yields no roster rather than a half-walked one (nothing is cached, so the next
caller retries), and that the merged roster the picker renders still resolves
when a vendor is down.

Docs-Skip: no doc covers the vendor's pagination; the reasoning is at the call
site and in the new spec.

subject: fix(llm): actually honour neverFallback, so a preview cannot lie
title: actually honour neverFallback, so a preview cannot lie
body:
Found by testing the preview against a model that does not exist. It returned
ok:true, because the fallback quietly answered from gpt-4o-mini instead:

  [LLM-FALLBACK] llm-preview: openai/gpt-4o-mini-does-not-exist failed
  (404 The model `gpt-4o-mini-does-not-exist` does not exist ...);
  retrying on openai/gpt-4o-mini

That is the exact failure `neverFallback` was added to prevent — a preview
reporting a model as working when nobody tested it, which is worse than an
error because it is believed. AI Lab runs had it too: a run of a named model
could be served by the tier default and reported as the chosen one.

Cause: when `neverFallback` moved off the dropped `llm_task_configs` column and
onto the registry row, `AiTaskService` read it (for display) and
`LlmCompletionService` never did. It passed `tier` into the resolver and
nothing else, so `fallbackEnabled` fell back to its permissive default. The
flag was correct, documented, displayed on the AI Tasks screen, and inert.

So both fields now come from ONE lookup, `callConfigForAiTask`. Fetching them
separately is precisely how the second got left out, and a single return makes
forgetting it impossible rather than merely discouraged.

The test gap was the same shape as the v1.84.2 one: every existing case mocks
the resolver, so they prove the service HONOURS `fallbackEnabled` while proving
nothing about where the value comes from. The new cases drive the real registry
and assert what reaches the resolver — verified by removing the wiring again
and watching three of them fail.

Verified in prod on 1.85.0 before this fix: gpt-4o-mini, claude-haiku-4-5 and
gemini-2.5-flash all preview correctly (201, "ok", real token counts), so the
llm-preview rewrite itself is sound; this is the one thing it surfaced. The
temporary catalog row used to probe it was deleted.

subject: fix(llm): stop the autofill rows advertising config nothing reads
title: stop the autofill rows advertising config nothing reads
body:
The autofill collapse left the three autofill rows pointing at
`openai.autofillModel` and naming ANTHROPIC_AUTOFILL_MODEL, neither of which
any call site reads any more — so the AI Tasks screen would have gone on
reporting the old default while the new AutofillService resolved through the
tier. That is the identical mistake the nine migrated services made one commit
earlier, which is the point: a hand-maintained registry drifts the moment the
code under it moves, and noticing twice by eye is not a control.

So the guard is widened from "no tiered row points at anthropic.* config" to
"no tiered row carries a configPath at all". A tiered row resolves through the
chain by definition, so any configPath on one is not merely dead but harmful —
AiTaskService falls back to it and prints a value nothing reads.

That wider assertion immediately caught a third case, and a different one:
`character-interview` had a tier it should never have had. It drives
AgentLlmProviderFactory directly rather than going through
LlmCompletionService, so `characterInterview.model` is genuinely what it reads.
The tier made this screen resolve it through a chain its call site does not
use, and the two would have diverged the moment anyone set
CHARACTER_INTERVIEW_MODEL. Tier removed, configPath kept, and the row now says
why it differs from its neighbours.

The autofill `detail` also claimed "a prompt-level Gemini provider is ignored:
there is no Gemini autofill executor". That was true of the old pair and is now
the opposite — the provider follows from the model id, so Gemini works.

subject: fix(auth): make email-based login lookups case/whitespace-insensitive (#461)
title: make email-based login lookups case/whitespace-insensitive (#461)
body:
A user (rekha.r@khpt.org) reported never receiving the OTP login email.
`generateOtpV2` and `validateUserAndIssueTokens` looked up the user by an
exact-match `email` column, but the submitted email is never normalised
(no @IsEmail/@Transform on the DTO, no citext column) while

arrived".

Normalise the submitted email (trim + lowercase) before the two
user-by-email lookups in AuthService, matching the normalisation already
applied on write.

behave like a real case-sensitive column match and submits an
email with different case/whitespace than the stored account. It fails on
current master (NotFoundException) and passes with this fix.

subject: fix(analytics): include the last day in filler quality dashboard windows
title: include the last day in filler quality dashboard windows
body:
FillerAnalyticsRepository.findingRates bound its inclusive `until` date
directly against a TIMESTAMP column with `occurredAt <= $2`. Postgres casts
a bare date literal like '2026-09-04' to midnight, so the comparison really
meant "before 2026-09-04 00:00:00" — silently dropping the entire final day
from every rolling range (today) and from any custom `to` date an admin
picked.

Widen the upper bound to the start of the following day so the whole
`until` day is included, matching how resolveWindow documents its
contract ("inclusive ISO date window").

Regression test in filler-analytics.repository.spec.ts pins the new
boundary and fails against the old `<=` comparison.

subject: fix(progress): close the daily XP/personal-best cap race
title: close the daily XP/personal-best cap race
body:
Two SCENARIO_SESSION_ENDED events for the same learner arriving close
together — plausible via the unfinalised-session sweeper, which emits
them with async:true in a loop that never waits on listeners — could
both read the same stale "already awarded today" total and both pass
the daily cap check, since xp_events' uniqueness constraint only
dedupes a repeated sourceId, not the day's running total.

Serialise the check-then-insert with a pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on
(userId, tenantId, awardedOn), following the same pattern already used
in RoadmapAllocationRepository.lockUserPeriod. Covered by two new
regression tests asserting the lock is taken before the cap read.

subject: fix(glossary): record a deferral when an accept fails the token cap
title: record a deferral when an accept fails the token cap
body:
adjudicateLanguage mutates verdict from 'accepted' to 'deferred' inside
the catch block of the accept path, but recordDeferral() only lived in
the sibling `else if (apply && verdict === 'deferred')` branch of the
if/else-if chain — which is evaluated once against the verdict at entry
and is therefore never reached after the mutation. So every
accept-then-cap-failure (the exact "glossary is full" scenario the
backoff feature exists for) left entry.adjudication.deferrals at 0
forever, meaning withinBackoff() always returned false and the
scheduler kept re-sending the same stuck proposal to the model every
hour — the runaway-cost behavior the backoff was built to stop.

Call recordDeferral() directly from the catch block so the deferral
streak advances on this path too.

Extended the existing 'defers when the cap still refuses after
re-tiering' test to assert entry.adjudication.deferrals is 1 after the
run; it failed with a TypeError (entry.adjudication was undefined)
before this fix.

subject: fix(glossary): overlay routing needs at least two profiles to mean anything
title: overlay routing needs at least two profiles to mean anything
body:
A proposal was routed to a variety-profile overlay whenever every supporting
tenant mapped to the same profile. With only one attached profile that
condition is a tautology: it reflects which tenants happen to send traffic, not
evidence that the rule is variety-specific.

Measured 2026-09-03: Tamil was the only language with a variety profile and had
exactly one (one tenant attached), so 65% of its published glossary -- 2,338 of
3,601 tokens -- had been routed into that single org's overlay, including
plainly universal Tamil grammar: animacy agreement, the dative case on
காத்திரு, colloquial conditional suffixes. Two consequences, both bad. A second
Tamil tenant would have inherited none of it. And the global glossary could
never grow, because every rule the language learned was routed away from it.
en/hi/mr/kn were unaffected -- they have no variety profiles at all.

Overlay routing now requires the language to have >= 2 attached profiles. Above
that threshold the single-profile signal is real: the other populations existed
and did not produce the error. Below it, everything routes global.

The existing spec fixture attached one profile, so it gains a second attached
tenant that contributes no annotations -- supplying the contrast without
changing which tenants support which proposal. New coverage asserts a
single-profile language routes everything global.

Prod data was corrected separately: `grammar` was the only Tamil section with
no global counterpart, so a global copy is now published. DEMCARES still sees
its overlay (which overrides) at 1325 Tier 0 tokens; a second Tamil org would
see 1224 rather than 636.

subject: fix(glossary): consume the evidence when a proposal restates a published rule
title: consume the evidence when a proposal restates a published rule
body:
A proposal matching published content hit `skippedDuplicates++; continue;` --
dropped, and its annotations never consumed. So the same rule was re-derived
from the same evidence and re-dropped on every cycle, forever, while those rows
occupied the bounded consolidation read window. glossary-dedupe.util documents
that loop as the cost of a WRONG suppression; for an ineffective published rule
it is not a wrong suppression, it is a permanent deadlock.

duplicateOf() now reports what matched and whether it came from published
content or a queued proposal, preferring published when both match -- the
caller's obligation is stricter there, so ambiguity should not resolve by
insertion order.

- A queued sibling is still dropped. It is undecided, and whichever of the two
  lands consumes the evidence.
- A published match records a batch engineering finding carrying the annotation
  ids. That consumes them, so the rule stops being re-derived, and it makes the
  collision visible: a published rule that keeps re-deriving is a rule that is
  not working.

subject: fix(builder): stop a green job counting as a shipped build
title: stop a green job counting as a shipped build
body:
`claude -p` exits 0 whenever the agent produces a final response, including
when it ends its turn mid-protocol. So "stopped after CODE without committing"
and "finished and opened PRs" were the same green job, and reconcile settled
both SUCCEEDED. The first real Builder build spent $16.77, opened no pull
request, and nothing reported it as a failure.

- The workflow gains an outcome gate, modelled on the one bug-fix-session.yml
  already has: read the run back after the engine exits, and if it is still
  QUEUED/RUNNING with no pause marker, say so precisely and go red. An
  unreachable ally-be is a reporting hiccup, not a failure, so it defers to
  reconcile.
- Reconcile no longer settles a callback-less success as SUCCEEDED. A run
  reports its own outcome or it did not finish. Pinned by a test; nothing
  covered this path before, which is why it stayed wrong.
- New GET runs/:runId/status so the gate has something to read.
- STACKS_API_KEY in the job env. The bridge was falling through to `gh auth
  token`, and BUILDER_GH_TOKEN has no `read:org`, so every build phase ran with
  no product guidance — the first real build's planner reported exactly that.
- HUSKY=0. The coder's per-commit eslint + jest --findRelatedTests duplicates
  the gate, which is the check `/complete` actually trusts.
- The event forwarder posts in chunks of 100. ally-be 400s above that and the
  forwarder does not retry a 4xx, so a busy phase silently dropped the whole
  queue — including the gate_result that `/complete {done}` refuses to finish
  without.

subject: fix(glossary): the adjudicator was shown the proposals as existing glossary
title: the adjudicator was shown the proposals as existing glossary
body:
The 14:00 UTC preview pass rejected ALL NINE queued proposals — every one —
with reason "3. RESTATES a rule already present", quoting each proposal's own
text back as the rule it supposedly restated:

  proposal: "- To form polite imperatives, use the suffix `-ங்க`..."
  reason:   RESTATES "- To form polite imperatives, use the suffix `-ங்க`..."

`summarizeGlossary` lists entries awaiting review under "(awaiting review,
also do not restate)". That is correct for CONSOLIDATION, which must not
re-propose what is already queued — one Tamil overlay had 11 queued and
invisible, which is why the listing was added. It is wrong for ADJUDICATION,
because the proposals being judged ARE the pending entries, so every proposal
appeared inside its own "existing glossary" block.

`includePending` now distinguishes the two callers, and both settings are
asserted in tests so a future change cannot quietly align them.

Two things worth recording about how this was found and caused:

Prompt v3 made it WORSE before it made it findable. The same five Tamil
proposals got 3 accepts under v2; under v3 they got 5 rejects, because v3
sharpened the restatement criterion and demanded a quote — and a
self-collision supplies an easy quote. Hardening a rule whose input is
contaminated amplifies the contamination.

The quote requirement is also the only reason this was diagnosable. v2's
reasons said "in the awaiting review section", which reads as a plausible
duplicate. v3 quoted the text, and the text was the proposal.

Preview mode is what kept this off production. In `apply` all nine would have
been permanently rejected — rejection consumes the evidence, so nothing
re-derives them — including three Tamil rules already verified sound by hand.

subject: fix(glossary): an empty consolidation run must still record a batch
title: an empty consolidation run must still record a batch
body:
The weekly cadence held for languages that produce batches and not at all for
languages that produce nothing. Observed 2026-09-02, after the cadence change
was live: en-IN, ta-IN and hi-IN went quiet as intended, while mr-IN and kn-IN
consolidated at 13:00 AND 13:30 — twice in half an hour on a supposedly
weekly interval.

Both the weekly interval and the 24h minimum gap are measured from the last
batch, and the `clusters.length === 0` path returned without writing one. So
the clock never advanced and every tick re-ran. It is self-perpetuating for
exactly the languages it hits: mr-IN and kn-IN have 1 and 3 unconsumed
annotations, all `fluency` below the systematicity bar, so they can never
cluster and therefore never create the batch that would slow them down.

This is the same shape as the original stall — a gate keyed on the wrong
thing — and it was invisible for the same reason: `batch=null` in the log
reads like "nothing happened", not "the clock is frozen".

An empty batch is also the honest audit record. "Ran, found nothing" is what
distinguishes a quiet loop from a stalled one, and not being able to tell
those apart is what hid the original stall for eight days.

No LLM spend is added: this path still returns before `resolvePromptByCode`.
Other early returns are safe — `unconsumed.length === 0` and the
`minAnnotations` skip are unreachable from the scheduler, and a parse failure
throws after the batch row already exists.

subject: fix(scribe): Handle a microphone disconnect once, not twice
title: Handle a microphone disconnect once, not twice
body:
handleConnection registered its own `client.on('disconnect')` on top of the
OnGatewayDisconnect hook Nest already calls, so every disconnect ran the handler
twice, concurrently. Both invocations read the session before either deleted it,
so both reached endChat and the loser failed with "Chat is not active" - which
the audit trail then reports as a failure to end a call that in fact ended
cleanly. Every mobile session on 21 Aug logged exactly two identical
CALL_END_FAILED entries, and chat 2540 ran handleChatEnded four times.

The manual listener is gone, and the session is claimed before the first await
so a genuinely doubled notification cannot reach endChat twice either.

subject: fix(roadmap): include the last day of a filed/released date range
title: include the last day of a filed/released date range
body:
`createdAt <= '2026-09-02'` casts to midnight in Postgres, so every row
filed on the 2nd fell outside a range that named the 2nd as its upper
bound. A range ending today reliably came back missing its newest rows,
which reads as the filter being broken rather than as an off-by-one.

Bare YYYY-MM-DD upper bounds now extend to the end of that day. Full
timestamps pass through untouched: @IsISO8601 accepts an instant, and a
caller who sent one has already said exactly where the bound is.
