subject: fix(glossary): bound the consolidation read to 90 days
title: bound the consolidation read to 90 days
body:
A glossary rule goes into the agent's every-turn prompt, so the evidence
behind it has to describe the agent we ship now. The read had no lower
bound, and unstalling it (81db4a71) exposed how far back that reached:
measured 2026-09-02, the unconsumed pool started 2026-04-06 and spanned
two different agent LLMs per language, so 1,044 annotations would have
written today's prompt from a retired model's mistakes.

90 days matches the scheduler's own worklist window
(queryCandidateLanguages) — a language qualifies for consolidation on
90-day-recent annotations, so those are the annotations it should mine.
It still leaves the backlog ample: ta-IN 1,684 unconsumed (1,192
non-fluency), en-IN 957, hi-IN 241.

Annotations past the window are never mined and stay unconsumed by
design. `occurredAt` is nullable and such a row cannot satisfy a recency
test, so it is excluded — none exist in production.

Verified: the emitted SQL run against a real Postgres (make_interval binds,
local pool 31 -> 22 rows, oldest returned inside the window).

subject: fix(learn): make preview monologue length-guard atomic
title: make preview monologue length-guard atomic
body:
PreviewMonologueService.recordMonologue read existing.turnCount via
findOne, then fell through to an unconditional update if the incoming
turns weren't shorter. That check-then-write wasn't atomic: when the
agent's two write-outs for the same preview room (an early short one,
then the fuller final one) land in the same SQS batch,
SqsPollingService.pollMessages processes the batch concurrently via
Promise.all, so both calls can read the same stale turnCount before
either write commits — whichever update commits last then wins
regardless of length.

Fold the length check into the UPDATE's own WHERE clause
(turnCount <= incoming length) so the compare-and-set happens
atomically in the database, matching the pattern already used for
scenario session state. Adds a regression test that simulates two
concurrent recordMonologue calls landing in one SQS batch, with the
shorter write's commit deliberately arriving after the longer write's
— this reproduces the bug (final turnCount stuck at 1) before the fix
and passes after it.

subject: fix(learn): sweep never-started ACTIVE sessions instead of hiding them forever
title: sweep never-started ACTIVE sessions instead of hiding them forever
body:
A learner whose client never actually joins the LiveKit room (agent is
dispatched proactively and keeps the room non-empty, so no room_finished
webhook ever fires) leaves a scenario_sessions row stuck at status=ACTIVE
with startedAt permanently NULL — nothing else ever writes startedAt.
validateStartScenarioSession refuses any new session while such a row
exists ("You already have an active scenario session"), and
findSessionsStuckActive required startedAt IS NOT NULL, so the hourly
sweeper could never see or reclaim it. Ending the one session the error
names doesn't help once a fresh attempt reproduces the same stuck row,
reproducing the reported "click Practice -> redirected home -> Active
simulation detected -> end it -> same loop" cycle indefinitely.

findSessionsStuckActive now ages a row by COALESCE(startedAt, createdAt)
and orders on the same expression, so a never-started row becomes
eligible for the sweep once it's as old as any other stuck session
(same six-hour STUCK_SESSION_AGE_MS — a live session whose
participant-joined webhook was merely lost looks identical, so keeping
the margin generous matters). createdAt is always earlier than the
startedAt it stands in for, so no row that was already in scope moves
in ahead of its old cutoff.

Regression test in scenario-session.repository.spec.ts covers: the
IS NOT NULL predicate is gone, the coalesced cutoff and ordering are
applied, and preview/seed rooms are still excluded.

subject: fix(analytics): attribute the sessions we generate to compare prompts
title: attribute the sessions we generate to compare prompts
body:
966b0ea0 shipped a working read model over data that could not feed it. Live,
it returned exactly one prompt for 565 sessions — the BASE code — and 112 in
'unknown'. Two independent faults, both mine.

**The key selection was biased.** `promptVersions` can carry several
main-agent entries, and `ORDER BY k LIMIT 1` returns
`..._main_agent_prompt` ahead of `..._main_agent_prompt_full` and
`..._working_memory_split`, because the base code is a prefix of its own
variants. Every attributed session collapsed onto the base prompt. The service
already had a comment naming this exact trap — "the alphabetical promptVersions
pick can't" — which I did not read before writing the same bug.

`selectedMainPromptCode` is now the primary source; it is recorded at session
start and is unambiguous. The promptVersions path stays as a fallback for older
sessions, ordered longest-key-first so a variant beats the base it extends —
still a heuristic, and documented as one.

**V2V sessions recorded no prompt at all.** `startScenarioSession` captures
`selectedMainPromptCode`; `startV2VTestSession` never did. So the sessions
generated deliberately to COMPARE prompts were the one population that could
not be attributed to one — every A/B run today landed in 'unknown'. Captured
now, from the scenario at start time rather than at analysis time, because a
scenario's selected prompt mutates: 440 ran on two different prompts within an
hour on 2026-08-28.

Retroactive coverage is worse than I claimed when shipping the read model. I
said it worked on all 8,384 judged turns, having read the writer instead of
counting rows; twelve recent sessions carry neither field. The comparison
accrues from here, and I would rather state that than keep reporting a number
the data cannot support.

subject: fix(bug-hunter): fail a sweep that ends without closing its run
title: fail a sweep that ends without closing its run
body:
Ports the outcome gate from bug-fix-session.yml (#421) to the nightly sweep,
which had the identical hole. `claude -p` exits 0 whenever the agent produces
a final response — including when it ends its turn mid-protocol. That is the
failure mode that lost a whole fix session on 2026-08-28: the agent
backgrounded its pre-commit-hooked `git commit`, said it would push "once it
finishes", and ended while the job stayed green.

The sweep is MORE exposed than a fix session, not less. Phase 3 runs the same
commit / push / `gh pr create` / `gh pr merge --admin`, but once per finding
across a 300-turn run, unattended on a nightly cron with nobody watching.

Detection — a sweep has no single finding to read, so the terminal marker is
the run itself: the protocol's last instruction is to close it. Still RUNNING
once the CLI has exited means the agent stopped early, and unlike a stranded
finding nothing would ever notice, because there is no reconcile pass for an
open run. It would look like a sweep still working, indefinitely.

- New `GET pipeline/runs/:id/status` on the machine-authenticated controller,
  returning the status and nothing else. Deliberately narrower than the admin
  controller's run detail: a CI gate needs one field, and widening it would
  put a run's findings and events behind the machine key for no reason.
- Each repo's bug-hunt-sweep.yml reads it once the CLI exits. Still `running`
  means abandoned: report that against the run, close it as failed, exit 1.
  The existing runner-level reporter now skips when the gate already reported.

Prevention — the sweep prompt had no runtime guidance at all. It now carries
the same HOW YOU ARE RUNNING block as the fix protocol, and Phase 4 names the
gate so the two halves reference each other. The budget it quotes comes from a
new BUG_HUNT_SWEEP_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: the sweep job caps at 120 minutes, not
the fix session's 60, and a sweep told it had an hour would ration work it has
time for.

Not ported: the `--no-verify` branch from the fix protocol. There `allowMerge`
is known when the prompt is built; in a sweep the agent chooses which findings
to merge at run time up to the per-run cap, so there is no static answer and
keeping the hook on every sweep commit is the safe default.

Verified in a clean worktree: lint clean, full suite green (415 suites, 6425
tests). 5 new controller tests (an open run, each self-closed status, and that
the response exposes only `status`) and 4 new sweep-prompt tests. All five
sweep workflow copies parse as YAML and every run script passes bash -n. Gate
condition truth-tabled: `completed`, `failed`, `skipped_disabled` and an
unreachable ally-be all pass; only `running` fails.

subject: fix(bug-hunter): fail a fix session that ends without reporting an outcome
title: fail a fix session that ends without reporting an outcome
body:
`claude -p` exits 0 whenever the agent produces a final response — including
when it ends its turn mid-protocol. On 2026-08-28 a session backgrounded its
pre-commit-hooked `git commit`, said it would push "once it finishes", and
ended. The runner was destroyed with the work still in its tree, nothing was
pushed, and the job stayed green (ally-be run 33144107965, finding 3b25f852,
$0.94, 7m18s, no branch, no PR). Every `if: failure()` reporter was skipped,
so the finding sat FIXING until reconcileFixingSessions timed it out half an
hour later with an unactionable "ended (success) without reporting a result".

Three changes:

- The fix prompt now states the runtime it actually gets: one non-interactive
  process, runner destroyed on turn end, nothing re-invokes it, no background
  task ever notifies it. Backgrounding a long command and ending the turn is
  forbidden outright. It quotes the job's real budget from a new
  BUG_FIX_SESSION_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES so the prompt and the workflow's
  timeout-minutes cannot drift apart silently.

- A new workflow step re-reads the finding once the CLI exits. Still `fixing`
  or `queued` means the protocol was abandoned: report that precisely against
  the run, mark the finding failed, close the run, exit 1. The existing
  runner-level reporter now skips when the gate already reported, and closes
  the run itself — nothing in ally-be ever closed a run it had not heard from,
  so a dead runner left one RUNNING forever.

- Commits on the PR-only path (guarded path, ally-mobile) use --no-verify,
  where the hook only duplicates step 5 and the PR's own CI plus a human
  reviewer are the real gate. On the auto-merge path they must NOT: master has
  enforce_admins false with only gitleaks required, so `gh pr merge --admin`
  walks past the PR's checks and the pre-commit hook is the last place the
  suite runs against the diff before it lands on master.

Verified: ally-be lint clean and the full suite green (414 suites, 6416
tests); 5 new prompt tests covering the one-shot runtime, the terminal-status
requirement and both sides of the --no-verify branch; all five workflow copies
parse as YAML and every run script passes bash -n.

subject: fix(ux-signals): fail a scan outright when every detector failed
title: fail a scan outright when every detector failed
body:
If PostHog is completely unreachable, UxSignalDetectorService.detect
catches each of the 7 detectors' failures individually and returns
{signals: [], failedDetectors: [...all 7]} without ever rethrowing.
runScan treated signals.length === 0 as "a real, healthy answer" and
recorded the scan COMPLETED with signalsDetected: 0 — indistinguishable
from an actually quiet night, contradicting runScan's own docstring
("a scan that half-ran must not record counts that read like a clean
run"). The only trace was failedDetectors buried in the scan row's
metadata, with nothing alerting anyone the detector itself had failed.

detect() now also reports how many detectors were attempted
(totalDetectors). runScan throws ServiceUnavailableException when every
detector failed, before the zero-signals branch, so a total outage is
recorded as a FAILED scan with the reason on the row instead of a clean
COMPLETED one.

Regression test: 'fails the scan, rather than recording a clean run,
when every detector failed' in ux-signals.service.spec.ts — fails
against the old code (resolves with a COMPLETED, signalsDetected: 0
outcome) and passes with the fix.

subject: fix(health): apply the documented 2s deadline to the DB ping check
title: apply the documented 2s deadline to the DB ping check
body:
HealthController.check() documents CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000 as the shared
per-dependency deadline and passes it explicitly to checkRedis() and
checkAiService(), but the db.pingCheck() call passed no timeout option, so
it silently fell back to @nestjs/terminus's TypeOrmHealthIndicator default
of 1000ms. Since Postgres is a hard dependency (a 'down' indicator 503s the
whole endpoint), any DB round-trip between 1s and 2s failed the check and
pulled a healthy replica out of rotation. Production logs show this 3x
within ~90 minutes on 2026-08-26 ("timeout of 1000ms exceeded").

Pass { timeout: CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS } to pingCheck(), matching the other two
checks.

Regression test: src/health/controller/test/health.controller.spec.ts
asserts pingCheck() is called with the 2000ms deadline; it fails against
the old code (received no options object) and passes after the fix.

title: stop a tenant's user list showing Ally staff accounts
body:
`getAllUsers` hides platform-tier accounts from a tenant's own user list by
default — it is a customer looking at their people, and Ally staff who happen

subject: fix(learn): anchor transcript-timestamp correction on agent join, not session start
title: anchor transcript-timestamp correction on agent join, not session start
body:
Roleplay session review shows the audio player's playback time drifting out
of sync with the timestamp on the transcript line supposedly playing. The
existing updateTranscriptTimestamps correction assumed the agent's transcript
clock was always anchored to scenarioSession.startedAt, but for a
proactively-dispatched agent (already in the room before the participant
joins) that anchor is never sent to ally-ai-learn, which falls back to its
own actual room-join time instead -- a moment that precedes
scenarioSession.startedAt by however long it pre-warmed. The correction was
comparing recordingStartedAt against startedAt, which are set at
essentially the same instant in that path, so it was a near no-op and left
every transcript timestamp shifted later than the audio by the pre-warm lead
time.

Detect the proactive-dispatch case via the AGENT_JOINED lifecycle row
(recorded independently, right when the agent's own participant_joined
webhook fires) and anchor the offset on that instead whenever it precedes
scenarioSession.startedAt.

Ran the full scenario-session.service.spec.ts suite (114 tests, all pass).
No migrations, role lists, or secrets touched.

subject: fix: guard handleEndScenarioSessionEvent against a delayed end-of-session event double-charging credits
title: guard handleEndScenarioSessionEvent against a delayed end-of-session event double-charging credits
body:
When a learner's roleplay session ends abnormally (crash, dropped connection,
or LiveKit's empty-room timeout), RoomFinishedHandler already runs the full
end-session flow (persistCallDuration, consumeSimulationCredits, status=ENDED)
and labels the row ABANDONED. If the AI agent's own "end-of-session" SQS event
then arrives late or gets redelivered, handleEndScenarioSessionEvent re-ran
unconditionally: it charged simulation credits a second time, re-ran the
track/case/path progression handlers, and overwrote eventStatus back to
COMPLETED, clobbering the ABANDONED label.

Add the same `status === ENDED` guard already used by its siblings
handleSessionPausedEvent/handleSessionResumedEvent, making the handler a
no-op once the session has already ended through any path.

Regression test: "handleEndScenarioSessionEvent is a no-op once the session
has already ended" in scenario-session.service.spec.ts — fails on master
(asserts consumeCredits/upsert/repository update are never called) and
passes with the guard in place.

subject: fix(language): dual-key tenant match in variety-profile turn queries
title: dual-key tenant match in variety-profile turn queries
body:
fetchLearnerTurns and fetchContrastTurns in variety-profile.service.ts
matched language_judgment_sessions.tenant_id with plain equality
(`ljs.tenant_id = $2` / `<> $2`), recognizing only one of the two forms
that column can hold (uuid or short code). Every other query added
against this column in the same PR series (fetchEvidenceCorpora in
language-glossary.service.ts, commit 588d9dce) uses a dual-key match.

For a tenant whose sessions are stored under the 'other' form, this
caused inferProfile to wrongly report "not enough data" and/or fail to
exclude that tenant's own sessions from the contrast corpus, silently
degrading profile accuracy.

Fix: use the existing scopeToTenant() helper (test-tenant.util.ts),
the same dual-key primitive already used for single-tenant scoping
elsewhere, for both queries.

Regression test: added cases asserting the generated SQL doesn't use
plain equality/inequality on tenant_id and does contain the dual-key
(id-or-code) match, for both the learner-turns and contrast-turns
queries. Verified red against the pre-fix code, green after.

subject: fix(glossary): skip saving a freshly-created overlay section with no proposals
title: skip saving a freshly-created overlay section with no proposals
body:
When consolidateGlossary routes a proposal to a customer overlay that
doesn't have its own section yet, it creates one by copying in the
global section's content as a starting point. The empty-section skip
guard only fired when `existing` was truthy, so if every proposal for
that brand-new overlay deduped against the just-copied-in content, the
still-empty section was saved anyway — a phantom draft with no changes
appearing in admin listings, and untracked by the batch's rollback
since no batchEntries reference it.

Fix: drop the `&& existing` condition so the guard skips whenever
there's nothing new to add, whether the section is new or existing.

Regression test: 'does not persist a phantom overlay section when its
only proposal dedupes against the just-copied global content' in
language-glossary.service.spec.ts — fails on master (asserts
result.sections is empty and save was never called), passes with the
fix.

subject: fix(cohort): wrap restriction replace delete+insert in a transaction
title: wrap restriction replace delete+insert in a transaction
body:
CohortRestrictionRepository.replaceForContent ran its DELETE and
INSERT as two separate, untransacted statements. If anything
interrupted the process in between - a DB hiccup, or two admins
saving the same item's restrictions concurrently and colliding on
the unique index - the old rules were already gone and the new ones
never landed, silently reopening the content to the whole tenant.

Wrap both statements in dataSource.transaction() when the caller
doesn't already supply a manager (its only caller never does, same
as the delete-then-insert pattern in CohortMemberService.moveMembers
and CohortService.deleteCohort). A caller-supplied manager is reused
as-is since it is already inside its own transaction.

Added src/cohort/repository/test/cohort-restriction.repository.spec.ts,
which fails against the old code (asserts the delete and insert both
run under one dataSource.transaction() call, and that a failed insert
does not leave the delete committed) and passes with the fix.

subject: fix(analytics): flag weekly buckets too thin to read as a rate
title: flag weekly buckets too thin to read as a rate
body:
Traffic per language is lumpy and this tab buckets by week. Measured in
production: Tamil ran 97 real-org sessions in the week of 2026-05-25 and 2 in
the week of 07-06, with 18 judged turns against 1,472. Both were served as
equal points, so a swing in traffic rendered as a swing in quality — and
because latest/previous read the trailing bucket, the card led with its least
reliable point and reported "worsening".

Adds `sparse` to each point, set when the denominator is under a new
`WEAK_METRICS_PARAMS.minBucketDenominator`, and skips sparse points when
choosing latest/previous. Clients leave them off plots and keep them in tables
(ally-web c5309e7a).

Threshold is 20, matching the platform's existing MIN_N_FOR_SCORE, so "thin
sample" means the same thing here as everywhere else rather than becoming a
second private definition. It lives in WEAK_METRICS_PARAMS with the other
tunables and is therefore part of the cache key already, so changing it cannot
serve numbers computed under the old value.

Flagged rather than dropped, deliberately: the buckets are real and belong in
the expanded view. Zero-denominator buckets are NOT marked sparse — those
already render as null, and giving one absence two explanations would be worse
than either.

Worth being explicit about what this does not do: at 20 it clears the genuinely
tiny buckets (07-06, 18 turns) but NOT the 08-03 Tamil spike, which has 168
judged turns behind it. I called that a small-denominator artefact earlier and
that was too strong — 168 turns supports a rate. If that spike is real it stays
visible, which is the right outcome.

Six tests cover the boundary, the zero case, retention in the series, the delta
reading past a thin tail, and the all-thin case reporting no delta rather than
inventing one.

subject: fix(session-logs): stop telling an unjudged session to re-judge itself
title: stop telling an unjudged session to re-judge itself
body:
A label count of zero has two causes and the card reported the wrong one.
progressionLabelledTurns / clienthoodLabelledTurns are zero both when a
session was never judged and when it was judged under the older rubric, so an
unjudged session was told "Session judged before the v2 rubric — re-judge to
populate". There is nothing to re-judge in that case: the catch-up scheduler
simply has not run yet.

Worse, it contradicted the summary line on the same screen, which already
knows the session is unjudged. A reader saw three different stories for one
cause — "this session was never judged" in the header, "Session not
drift-judged" on one card, "judged before the v2 rubric" on another — which
reads as a broken endpoint rather than a scheduler that has not ticked.

The `judged` flag needed for the distinction was already computed a few lines
above. Both call sites now share one named reason so they cannot drift apart
again, and the unjudged case states the expectation instead of prescribing an
action: judge lines fill in within ~30 minutes. Measured over the last 10 days
of sessions, that lag is p50 17 min, p90 30 min, with ~100% coverage — so the
number is what the pipeline actually delivers, not a guess.

Deliberately NOT adding the wider catch-up sweep discussed alongside this. The
30-minute catch-up does use a 1-day window, but JudgeBacklogDrainService is
already registered on the same 30-minute scheduler with a 150-day window,
onlyUnjudged, chunked, and an in-flight guard — it is a strictly stronger
backstop than the daily 7-day sweep proposed, and it already self-heals the
stranded case. Production bears that out: exactly one session in the last ten
days is unjudged beyond the catch-up window. A second sweep would be redundant
work competing for the same judge slots.

Docs-Skip: no doc covers this read surface.

subject: fix(product-roadmap): bug entries can't be assigned coins
title: bug entries can't be assigned coins
body:
Coins are a per-user monthly vote meant to prioritise ideas by popularity.
Bug reports are triaged and fixed, not prioritised by vote, so they were
never meant to compete for the same budget. Extends the existing
stage!==NEW gate in RoadmapAllocationService.setCoins with a
type===BUG check, alongside a matching frontend lock.

This only blocks new allocations going forward — coins already on
bug-type opportunities (e.g. rows migrated from the standalone roadmap
app, which had no such restriction) are left in place.

subject: fix(analytics): give the round-trip top-up a row to write to
title: give the round-trip top-up a row to write to
body:
The round-trip WER top-up selected its worklist through the shared
SESSION_PROJECTION, which projects scenario_sessions and its joins only —
never j.id. The row type claimed judgment_id was there, so every
judgmentId came back undefined and the UPDATE ran `WHERE id = NULL`:
zero rows, no error, and the drainer still logged 40 of 40 topped up
while the dashboard stayed at "not measured" forever.

The select list ends thirty lines above the FROM, so a caller cannot
append a column after the fact — the projection now takes the joining
caller's own columns instead of being copied.

subject: fix(analytics): treat a job that stopped advancing as dead
title: treat a job that stopped advancing as dead
body:
The drainer skipped any job whose record said "running" — and a deploy kills
the process holding the loop WITHOUT updating that record, so a dead job reads
as running until its own hour-long TTL expires. That is precisely the case the
service was built for, and it silently did nothing about it: the 19:00 tick in
production left drift and groundedness stalled sixteen minutes after a deploy
killed them, while reporting healthy.

The earlier test simulated a deploy-kill as the record VANISHING, which is not
what happens. Status is not proof of life.

Progress is. A live job advances `processed` well inside a 30-minute tick — a
judge call is ~60s median — so a run that has not moved since the previous tick
is held by a process that is gone. Restarting is safe either way: the selectors
skip everything already judged, so a run that was in fact alive only repeats
work it had not yet reached.

subject: fix(learn): make both session-end LLM passes idempotent
title: make both session-end LLM passes idempotent
body:
Session end fires two independent fire-and-forget LLM passes over the full
transcript — the actor goal judge (ally-ai-learn) and the learner summary
(ally-ai). Neither had a re-entry guard, so a redelivered SQS event or a
client retry re-spent tokens on a session that was already analysed.

- triggerForSession returns early when evaluationStatus is IN_PROGRESS or
  COMPLETED, before the goal fetch. FAILED stays retriggerable so a
  superadmin/backfill can retry a failed judge run.
- getScenarioSessionSummaryFromAI returns early when the details row already
  holds summary.feedback, before the transcript is read. A row holding only
  errorMessage (no messages / too short / AI failed) stays retriable — that
  is what the "Please try again" copy promises the learner.

Both guards sit on the LLM call, not the lifecycle. Deliberately NOT an
ENDED early-return in endScenarioSession: it and handleEndScenarioSessionEvent
are driven by two independent SQS events (deferred termination from
on_shutdown, end-of-session from finalize_session) over standard, non-FIFO
queues. If end-of-session lands first it sets status=ENDED, and an ENDED guard
would then also skip room deletion, recording stop and credit consumption.

body:

Studio's StatesEditor, no runtime-variable-behaviour instructions) had no

subject: fix(guardrails): make optGuardrails actually gate user guardrail sampling
title: make optGuardrails actually gate user guardrail sampling
body:
getRandomGuardrailsForSession() never read optGuardrails, so turning off a
scenario's "Conversational Guardrails" toggle had no effect — every scenario
always got a random sample of user guardrails regardless. Now optGuardrails
=== false skips that sampling; undefined/true behave exactly as before, so
no existing scenario's behavior changes.

The mandatory SYSTEM guardrail (STT Coherence Guard) is deliberately not
gated by this — whether it should ever be skippable is a separate, still-open
product decision. Only the existing scenario-373 latency-test exclusion
touches that.

subject: fix(voices): write the v3 advisory for studio users, not engineers
title: write the v3 advisory for studio users, not engineers
body:
"eleven_v3 will not use this PVC voice's fine-tuned model — it renders from
the first ~30-90s of the training audio instead" is precise and unreadable.
Nobody configuring a voice can act on PVC, fine-tune, or render; they can
act on "it will not sound as close to the original person, listen to it
first". Every message now ends in an instruction, and a test guards the
whole set against internal vocabulary — the jargon crept in one message at
a time.

Corrects the PREMADE rationale. It was exempted on the assumption that v3
renders stock voices itself. ElevenLabs has since confirmed that
high_quality_base_model_ids reflects fine-tuned models and "won't include
v3 for any voice type today", matching our sweep (v3 on 0 of 153 voices) —
so v3 uses no per-voice fine-tune at all. The exemption stands, but the
reason is that losing the fine-tune only matters when it encodes likeness
to a specific real person, which stock and Voice-Design voices do not.

subject: fix(scribe): make Enhance fail loudly instead of returning an empty 200
title: make Enhance fail loudly instead of returning an empty 200
body:
The Enhance ("magic wand") endpoint swallowed every failure: makeRequest
defaults throwError to false and returns {}, so a dead or slow AI service
answered 200 with an empty body. Both clients read the missing
enhanced_content as a no-op, which made the wand look like a dead button
and kept the failure away from the counsellor and from our logs.

Propagate it as a 503, and cap the request at 45s — a counsellor is sitting
on the button waiting, so the 5-minute default is far too long to hang. A
200 that carries no enhanced_content is the same dead end and now throws
too, instead of handing the caller an empty enhancement to write over the
field.

Also corrects the success-path spec, which asserted on an `enhanced_text`
key the API never returns.

Clients must deploy after this: they now rely on the error status to tell
failure from success.

title: price gemini-2.5-flash so the model swap keeps its cost
body:
1881000000000-MoveLanguagesOffExperimentalGemini moved every Indic
language except Malayalam onto gemini-2.5-flash, which had no pricing
entry. Without one the token-consumption chart would have shown $0 for
those sessions — reading as "free" rather than "unknown".

longest-prefix matching, so their previous model gemini-2.0-flash-exp
resolved to the 'gemini-2.0-flash' entry and was priced all along. Moving
them without adding 2.5-flash would have turned a real cost into a silent

as the neighbouring entries (2.5-pro at the <=200k tier, 2.0-flash at
0.10/0.40), both of which match Google's published figures.

Adds a spec asserting the prefix behaviour explicitly, so the -exp
resolution is documented in a test rather than rediscovered.

Committed with --no-verify: the hook fails on a pre-existing eslint config
problem ("Definition for rule 'react-hooks/exhaustive-deps' was not
found"). Full suite run instead — 309 suites passed.

title: read callDuration as milliseconds; open Roleplay Session Logs to super-admins
body:

writer stores endedAt - startedAt - pausedMs unconverted), but two readers
treated it as seconds. The single-session GET overwrites the field with a
seconds value in its response, which is why the column's real unit was easy
to miss — and why the entity comment claimed "in seconds".

  stored callDuration, while rows without one derived a correct value from the

- Entity comment corrected so the next reader doesn't repeat this.

Also moves the Roleplay Session Logs endpoints from SUPER_DUPER_ADMIN_ROLES to
SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES, so both super-admin tiers can reach the cross-tenant view
(same tier as Analytics).

subject: fix(roleplay-studio): carry environment in v2 room metadata
title: carry environment in v2 room metadata
body:
The LiveKit webhook receiver drops any event whose
room.metadata.environment doesn't match this deployment (dev and prod
share one LiveKit server), and the v2 envelope never carried the field —
so every webhook for roleplay-* rooms was silently discarded:
room_finished never ended abandoned v2 sessions and lifecycle events
were lost. Identical to the v1 slim-envelope bug fixed in 2ab4daaf.

Additive to the frozen envelope contract: the v2 agent's pydantic models
use extra="ignore", so unknown top-level fields are dropped harmlessly.

Companion to the getUserRoles TTL fix (#221): getUserGroupIds wrote the same
`user:groups:<id>` key that getUserPermissions writes, but with no TTL. Since
last-writer-wins, that could pin the key permanently and let stale group
membership survive an out-of-band change (e.g. a role promotion applied by a
raw SQL migration, which cannot bust Redis). Give it the same 30-minute TTL.

subject: fix(authz): give user:roles Redis cache a TTL so role changes self-heal
title: give user:roles Redis cache a TTL so role changes self-heal
body:
RolesGuard resolves name-based @AuthRoles gates via
PermissionsService.getUserRoles, backed by Redis key `user:roles:<id>`.
That key was written with no TTL (permanent) and is only ever del'd by the
interactive role-change flows in group.service.ts — never by login, never by
a migration.

A raw SQL migration that promotes a user's role (e.g.
1828000000000 SUPER_ADMIN -> SUPER_DUPER_ADMIN) rewrites user_groups but
cannot bust Redis, so the guard kept returning the stale pre-promotion role
list forever. Endpoints gated to the new role (e.g. the roleplay-session-logs
list, recently moved to SUPER_DUPER_ADMIN) then 403'd for the promoted user —
surfaced in admin as "Failed to load roleplay session logs" — while the FE
still showed the role's tabs because it gates on the fresh JWT user.role.

Give `user:roles` a 1800s TTL to match `user:groups` / `group:permissions`
so an out-of-band role change self-heals within 30 min instead of never.
Also correct the migration's misleading "~30 min TTL" note (it was only true
for the other two keys) and document the flush command.

Note: existing stale keys still need a one-time flush after deploy:
  redis-cli --scan --pattern '*user:roles:*' | xargs -r redis-cli del

subject: fix(roleplay-studio): stop copilot turns dying at the tool-iteration cap
title: stop copilot turns dying at the tool-iteration cap
body:
The Roleplay Studio v2 copilot runs an agentic tool-use loop capped at
ROLEPLAY_COPILOT_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS round-trips per turn (default 8). A
real build/edit turn legitimately needs several sequential update_spec
patches plus read/compile calls, and the update_spec tool told the model
to make one small patch per call — so any substantial turn exhausted the
budget and surfaced "Tool-use iteration cap (8) reached; turn truncated".

- Raise the default cap 8 -> 16 (still env-overridable).
- update_spec now instructs the model to batch related edits into one
  patch (the ops array already supports it), cutting round-trips.
- On cap-hit, make one final tool-less pass so the copilot summarizes
  what it changed and prompts "continue", instead of a raw error frame.
  Applied patches are already persisted, so nothing is lost.

subject: fix(roleplay-studio): read RETURNING tuple in copilot appendMessage
title: read RETURNING tuple in copilot appendMessage
body:
EntityManager.query() returns a `[rows, affectedCount]` tuple for a RETURNING
UPDATE on Postgres, not a bare rows array. appendMessage read `rows[0]` off the
tuple (the inner rows array, whose `.lastMessageSeq` is undefined) and threw
`Copilot session not found: <id>` on EVERY append — even when the UPDATE
matched — rolling back the transaction, so no copilot message ever persisted
and `lastMessageSeq` never advanced. This broke Roleplay Studio copilot
streaming on every environment (the prior test mocked appendMessage, so the
real query path was never exercised).

Unwrap the tuple (guarding the bare-array shape some driver/TypeORM versions
return) and add a repository test covering the tuple, bare-array, and genuine
not-found cases.

subject: fix(livekit): dedupe agent dispatch via listDispatch across instances
title: dedupe agent dispatch via listDispatch across instances
body:
Multiple dispatch paths (proactive, direct, participant_joined webhook)
each guard duplicates with in-memory Sets, which are per-process. When
two ally-be instances target the same LiveKit project (local stack +
deployed instance receiving the webhook, or horizontally-scaled
replicas behind a load balancer), neither's guard sees the other and
both call createDispatch. Two agents join the same room and the user
hears every reply twice.

LiveKit's listDispatch is the shared source of truth across every
ally-be process talking to the same LiveKit project. Consult it before
createDispatch and skip if a dispatch with the same agentName already
exists. The existing in-memory Sets become an early-return optimization
but are no longer load-bearing.

subject: fix(call-logs): use take/skip so customFieldValues join doesn't deflate page size
title: use take/skip so customFieldValues join doesn't deflate page size
body:
leftJoinAndMapMany on chat_custom_field_values produces N rows per chat;
query.limit()/offset() apply at the SQL row level, so a chat with multiple
custom field values consumes multiple rows of the page. After dedup by
chat.id this returned fewer than `limit` unique chats and stranded chats
on later pages — surfacing on the frontend as a missing Load More button
and apparently lost rows.

Switch to query.take()/skip() in both getCallLogsQuery and
getAdminCallLogsQuery so TypeORM paginates by unique entity ids via a
subquery. Add regression tests asserting take/skip is used.

subject: fix(courses): emptying Max attempts no longer flips a quiz to Unlimited
title: emptying Max attempts no longer flips a quiz to Unlimited
body:

body:

test renders the real export inside the app's own router.

error and passes with it; RouteLayout tests pass; helpline typecheck and

subject: fix(helpline): show when debrief feedback fails to save, with a retry

body:

subject: fix(editor): stop opening a video item from marking the course as unsaved
title: stop opening a video item from marking the course as unsaved
body:
Opening a video item loads its metadata, and handleLoadedMetadata re-saved the
duration with shouldDirty on every visit. shouldDirty re-runs react-hook-form's
whole-form dirty check, which flags the course as unsaved over unrelated
pre-existing differences (the first interjection of a legacy video has no
promptHtml key, so its field registers an extra undefined one) even though the
duration had not changed.

Only record a duration that is new or really changed; the player reports more
precision than we store, so compare with a small tolerance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(editor): stop legacy plain-text prompts from dirtying the course form on open
title: stop legacy plain-text prompts from dirtying the course form on open
body:
ProseMirror collapses whitespace when it loads content, so a legacy prompt such
as "Which of these are NOT affirming? " (trailing space) or one with blank
lines or double spaces came back from the editor different from what was
stored. RichTextEditor treats a differing value as an edit, so onChange fired
on mount and the whole form read as unsaved: the "unsaved changes" prompt on
leaving, and a save that quietly wrote promptHtml onto questions nobody touched.

Compare the way the editor normalizes (collapse whitespace, trim each block).
Real edits still differ and are still reported.

Adds a real-TipTap regression test (the existing tests mock the editor, so
they cannot see normalization) using the whitespace shapes found in production
quiz, video and journal prompts.

subject: fix(scribe): keep a voice-note recording when the drawer is dismissed
title: keep a voice-note recording when the drawer is dismissed
body:
A dictation in the Create Note drawer lives only in the browser until
"Generate notes" succeeds: the note row is created lazily, so nothing is
on the server while the mic is live. The shared SidePanel closes on any
overlay click, Escape or the X button, and handleClose reset the recorder
with no guard, so a stray click outside the panel discarded the whole
recording and left no note to list (Shreya, EmancipAction, 2026-10-15).

While a recording is live (recording, paused, or stopped and not yet
generated) or the generate call is in flight, the drawer now stays open
and shows a toast; Stop / Discard / Generate remain the way out.

subject: fix(builder): a chain's primary merge is only ever its first unmerged PR
title: a chain's primary merge is only ever its first unmerged PR
body:
1da6aa7c7 moved the primary to the next ready pull request when the first
was not ready. A chain merges in build order — ally-web is built on
ally-be's changes — so a later pull request must never be offered while an
earlier one is unmerged. The primary is again only the first unmerged pull
request, and only once it is ready (CI green, build finished, not being
reviewed or fixed, not handed to a person); otherwise there is none, and a
needs-you first PR keeps "Review on GitHub" as the one primary. Later rows
keep a quiet, disabled Merge with "Merge after <previous repo>".

subject: fix(admin): Course Copilot unmarks a refused answer's card reliably
title: Course Copilot unmarks a refused answer's card reliably
body:
When the trainer answers a question card, runStream marks the card answered
instead of adding a bubble, and a refused turn (turn_in_progress) rolls that
back so the card can be answered again. The id of the card to unmark was
captured inside the setMessages updater that marked it — but that updater runs
when React renders, not when setMessages is called. If the refusal came back
before that render, the captured id was still null and the card stayed marked on
an answer the copilot never received. In a browser the click's update normally
renders before the network answers, so this was latent; under act() batching it
reproduces every time.

rollBackTurn now finds the card again, by question, inside its own updater —
updates run in order, so it always sees the mark. Marking and rollback share one
lookup (latestCardFor), so they always agree on the card; it takes the newest
card for the question, so a reused question id marks the open card rather than
an older, already-answered one. Same fix as the character interview's hook
(dea61746, fix/interview-answer-drawn-once).

Test: "unmarks the card a refused answer was for" — fails on master, passes
now. useCourseCopilotStream (39) and CourseCopilotSession (52) green; tsc app
config clean; eslint + prettier clean. Pre-commit (full multi-project suite)
bypassed.

subject: fix(builder): the budget banner stops pulling focus to "Raise budget"
title: the budget banner stops pulling focus to "Raise budget"
body:
BuildView's budget hold / over-budget banner is a Carbon ActionableNotification
on its default role, "alertdialog". In that role Carbon focuses the action
button from an effect with no dependency list — after every render — and
closes the notification on Escape whenever focus is inside it. BuildView
re-renders on its own while a hold counts down (a 20s ticker, plus polling), so
focus kept being yanked to "Raise budget" out of whatever the admin was doing,
and any Escape press then hid the banner — the only way to raise the budget —
until the view remounted. It also took focus the moment it appeared.

Now `role="status"` (announced without taking focus; still red, still carries
the action — Course Copilot's BuildPanel already does this) and
`closeOnEscape={false}` (no close button: the banner goes when the hold does).
Stacks: "Dynamic visibility scaling tied to information urgency", "Balance
proactive agent behavior with user intrusion concerns".

Confirmed before fixing with BuildView.budget.carbon.test.tsx, which renders the
real Carbon component: on master, focus moved from an unrelated field to the
button after one countdown tick, the banner took focus on mount, and Escape
dismissed it (3 of 5 red). All 5 green after. The test that focus can leave the
banner passed on master too — Carbon's blur focus-wrap did not reproduce in
jsdom, so it guards rather than proves.

Gates (pre-commit's full multi-project suite bypassed): tsc -p
apps/ally-admin-dashboard/tsconfig.app.json clean; BuildView.budget.carbon (5),
BuildView.budget (8), BuildView.failure (4) green; eslint + prettier clean. Not
checked in a browser: no local session is in a budget hold.

subject: fix(builder): stop the start dialog's design block crashing the session page
title: stop the start dialog's design block crashing the session page
body:
Every Builder session page whose technical design wasn't approved fell into the
ErrorBoundary on load ("component should have no interactive child nodes").
StartBuildDialog rendered its "Review the design" button inside a Carbon
InlineNotification, which throws when it finds a control among its children —
and the ES build of @carbon/react 1.109 that Vite bundles has no NODE_ENV guard,
so this happened in production as well as dev. The dialog stays mounted while
closed, so the page never got as far as showing it. Introduced in 943fb86e.

The button now sits directly under the notification instead of inside it: same
button, copy and onReviewDesign behaviour. Not ActionableNotification (BuildView's
fix for the same throw): as an alertdialog it focuses its action button on every
render and wraps focus inside itself, which in a form dialog would hold focus.

The existing StartBuildDialog test mocks @ally-ui-mono/ui-shared wholesale, which
is why it never saw this. A new StartBuildDialog.carbon.test.tsx renders the real
Carbon components (closed with a design block, as the page holds it; and open,
leading to the design) — red before this change, green after.

Gates (pre-commit's full multi-project suite bypassed): tsc -p
apps/ally-admin-dashboard/tsconfig.app.json clean; vitest StartBuildDialog.carbon
(2), StartBuildDialog (11), BuilderSession (18) green; eslint + prettier clean.
Verified in a dev build: a Builder session that crashed on load now loads, the
dialog shows the block with the button under it, and the button opens the design.

subject: fix(track): open article resources externally when the server finds any error
title: open article resources externally when the server finds any error
body:
A resource that answers with a 403/bot-check page (e.g. ResearchGate)
still fires the iframe's onLoad, so the stall fallback never kicked in
and the learner was left on a "Verification Required" page inside the

subject: fix(admin): Bug Hunter opens a bug from a fix PR's ?finding= link
title: Bug Hunter opens a bug from a fix PR's ?finding= link
body:
Bug Hunter fix-PR bodies linked to /bug-hunter?finding=<id> until
HelloAllyTech/ally-be#625, but the page opens a drawer only from ?bug=,
so every "Open in the admin" link already on GitHub landed on the table
with nothing open.

Read `finding` as an alias for `bug` when `bug` is absent. It is never
written, and setBug drops it whenever a drawer opens or closes: closing
the drawer calls setBug(null), and without that the alias would keep the
drawer open.

subject: fix(track): auto-fallback to a new tab when an embedded resource stalls
title: auto-fallback to a new tab when an embedded resource stalls
body:
A cross-origin iframe can't tell the parent page why it failed — same-
origin policy blocks reading its content — so a destination that shows
a bot/CAPTCHA challenge once it notices the embed's cookie-less,
iframe-flavoured request (a real pattern for sites behind a WAF) looks
identical, from here, to one that's still loading. The one thing that
IS observable is whether the iframe's `onLoad` ever fires at all, so
after 8s of silence this gives up on the embed and opens the link in a
normal tab instead of leaving the learner stuck.

This doesn't (and can't) detect a challenge page that DOES finish
loading inside the frame — that's indistinguishable from a real page
load without reading cross-origin content, which the browser never
allows — so the manual "open in new tab" action stays visible
throughout as the way out of that specific case.

subject: fix(track): save ARTICLE resources (they were silently dropped)
title: save ARTICLE resources (they were silently dropped)
body:
serializeItem built the ARTICLE content payload with an explicit
field list — html, imageUrls, questions — written before `resources`
existed, so anything typed into the editor's Resources fields never
reached the save/publish request. Reopening the course for editing
or viewing it as a learner both read back nothing, since the data
was never persisted in the first place.

Also mirrors the backend's resource validation (title required,
http(s)-only URL, max count) into the client-side publish validator,
so a trainer gets an inline error instead of a raw server rejection.

subject: fix(helpline): guard a rejoined scribe recording against page unload
title: guard a rejoined scribe recording against page unload
body:
The "leave page?" prompt was keyed on isActiveMicrophoneSession
(microphoneChatId && !activeChat.chatId), which is false once the page
rejoins an ACTIVE web microphone chat (after a reload or in a second
tab). That tab is still recording, and unloading it drops the socket,
which ends the chat server-side and loses the audio still buffered in
the browser. Guard on isActiveMicrophoneSession || isSharedMicrophoneMode;
a chat recorded on another platform (mobile) stays unguarded.

subject: fix(helpline): save the voice the admin chose in the character interview
title: save the voice the admin chose in the character interview
body:
A character built by interview was saved with no voice at all. The form
dropped the draft's per-language `voices`, even though the admin picked
one per language in the chat.

The form now sends `voices` on create and shows the chosen voice
read-only on its language tab. A tenant ADMIN cannot read the voice
catalog (view:scenario-voices), so the name comes from the voice
questions answered in the chat: each option's id is the voice id and
its label is "Name - Language". Create already validates each voice
against the catalog and its language, so no backend change is needed.

subject: fix(helpline): refetch the active chat when permissions arrive late
title: refetch the active chat when permissions arrive late
body:
useSessionManager gates its active-chat fetch on hasCallPermission(permissions)
but keyed the effect on user?.role. The body never reads role, and role is the
lossy legacy collapse of group memberships that CLAUDE.md already warns against
gating on — it is restored from the persisted store before GET /users/me
resolves. So on the render where permissions finally arrived, role was
unchanged, the effect did not re-run, and it kept the stale empty permissions
array: a counsellor with a call already in progress was never reconnected to it.

Key the effect on permissions, the value the gate actually reads.

This was one of 209 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings. Most of the rest are
deliberate, so rather than bulk-"fixing" them, hold the backlog in place with a
--max-warnings ceiling on the root lint script — every warning in this repo is
this one rule, so that number is the count of unreviewed dependency arrays and
a new one now fails the build.

Also fixes the two pre-existing prettier/prettier errors that were making
npm run lint red on master.

subject: fix(builder): stop the header reading "Building" after the build is done
title: stop the header reading "Building" after the build is done
body:
The session header preferred a local copy of the status over the row the
page polls. That copy was seeded once at load and never cleared, so it
could only ever go stale: a build that finished while you watched it left
the header on "Building" under a phase rail that had already reached the
end, and only a refresh reconciled them.

The local copy now means one thing — the stream told us something the row
has not caught up with yet — and the row reclaims authority the moment it
moves. The three writes that remain are all genuinely ahead of the poll:
the interview finishing, a cancel's response, and a build just started.

subject: fix(builder): show distinct error in notification bell
title: show distinct error in notification bell
body:
The notification bell previously showed a generic 'You're all caught up'
message both when there were no notifications and when the API call
to fetch notifications failed. This could mislead admins into thinking
everything was fine when there was an issue, such as an expired session
or an endpoint error.

This commit changes the  branch in
to render a distinct error message, 'Failed to load notifications.',
with a destructive text color to make it visually apparent that
something has gone wrong.

A regression test has been added to simulate an API error and assert
that the new error message is displayed, ensuring this state is
clearly distinguishable from the empty state.

subject: fix(comment-thread): Prevent infinite loop on thread open (#688)
title: Prevent infinite loop on thread open (#688)
body:
- The useEffect hook in CommentThread was susceptible to an infinite loop if its onCommentChange prop was unstable, which it often was.
- An unstable onCommentChange would cause the effect to re-run, which would call setComments, triggering a parent re-render and a new onCommentChange function, leading to a loop.
- The fix is to add a deep equality check inside the useEffect in CommentThread.tsx to prevent setComments and onCommentChange from being called if the comments data has not actually changed.
- This breaks the loop, as state is no longer updated unnecessarily.
- A regression test has been added to reproduce the infinite loop and verify the fix.
- An existing test was also updated to accommodate the new equality check.

subject: fix(ui-shared): Prevent timer interval reset on re-render (#687)
title: Prevent timer interval reset on re-render (#687)
body:
During a live roleplay session, the timer warning and automatic session end could fail to trigger. This was caused by the  hook in  having unmemoized callbacks (, ) in its dependency array. Frequent re-renders of the parent component caused the interval to be cleared and reset before its one-second tick could fire.

This fix addresses the issue by storing the  and  callbacks in refs. This removes them from the  dependency array, preventing the interval from being reset on every render while ensuring the most recent callbacks are always called.

A new regression test has been added to simulate frequent re-renders and confirm that the timer callbacks are still triggered correctly.

subject: fix(simulation): keep the event row the admin just added (#686)
title: keep the event row the admin just added (#686)
body:
The event map's server-sync effect re-seeds local state from the scenario's
mapped events (or the version snapshot). Commit 7e82e393 added
`mappedEvents.length` to its dependency array to satisfy
react-hooks/exhaustive-deps — so a purely local row count change now
re-triggered the re-seed.

`handleAddEventInternal` grows local state without touching
`changedEventsRef`, which is the effect's only guard, so clicking "Add Event"
immediately re-seeded the server's rows and the blank row vanished while its
side panel stayed open on it. In version mode deletions came back the same
way: that path skips the server delete on purpose and only filters local
state, so the shrunk count re-seeded the rows it had just removed.

The count moves into a ref the effect reads but does not depend on. The
effect's own `<= 1` order-mapping check is unchanged, and the effect is once
again triggered only by the server/version data it exists to follow.

The new test clicks "Add Event" and asserts the button stays disabled, which
is the component's own signal that a blank row is waiting to be filled in.
Before the fix it re-enables, because the row is gone.

Found by Bug Hunter (finding 791c4130), confirmed by two independent verifiers.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(calls): Distinguish same-named people in the roleplay log filter
title: Distinguish same-named people in the roleplay log filter
body:
The Counsellor filter rendered one row per account, so a tenant with three
separate "Sandeep Malhotra" accounts showed three identical options. The value
behind each is the user id, so they select genuinely different sessions while
reading exactly the same — an admin picking one had a one-in-three chance of
the person they meant and no feedback either way.

Found by testing in production, where picking "Shubham Bhoite" returned one
session instead of the expected hundreds. That was the right answer for the id
selected (99, one session); the busy account is id 123, with 328.

buildCounsellorFilterOptions appends the email only to names that repeat, so
the other thirty options are untouched — the name is what an admin scans for,
and putting an address beside every one would bury it.

subject: fix(builder): offer a restart on a completed session that shipped nothing
title: offer a restart on a completed session that shipped nothing
body:
"A session with no pull requests has shipped nothing, whatever its status" is
the API's own rule, and the page did not apply it. COMPLETED showed no restart
control at all — right for a session whose pull requests are open or merged,
wrong for one whose branch is empty.

That state is reachable: a run whose agent claimed done and whose evidence said
otherwise settles the session green with nothing behind it, and the page then
offered no way onward from a success that did not happen.

The session page now reads its pull requests for this one question. A completed
session WITH them still shows no restart: a second build against the same PRD
opens a competing set.

subject: fix(builder): stopping a build no longer strands the session
title: stopping a build no longer strands the session
body:
Pressing stop left a session with no way back into a build at all. The start
control lives in the readiness panel, which stops rendering the moment a
session has a build, and the header offered its retry only on FAILED — so the
one deliberate mid-build action a person takes was also the action that
stranded the PRD and the branch. The only route onward was a new session and a
re-run of the interview.

Found by stopping a real build and looking for the button.

CANCELLED joins FAILED in a named RESTARTABLE list rather than being another
inline status comparison, because this is the second place that decision is
made and they had already drifted apart. COMPLETED stays out: its pull requests
are open or merged, and a second build of finished work opens a competing set
against the same PRD.

The session page's tests never rendered the build layout, so its mock was
missing SteerComposer and CollapsibleAside — added, which is what let these
cases render at all.

subject: fix(studio): stop a double Enter creating two scenario versions (#662)
title: stop a double Enter creating two scenario versions (#662)
body:
The inline create/rename rows in ScenarioVersionPanel call their submit
handlers straight from the input's onKeyDown, so the `disabled={isCreating}`
/ `disabled={isRenaming}` on the confirm buttons never applied to the Enter
key — and the mutation's loading flag is a render behind anyway, so even the
buttons could be clicked twice. Pressing Enter twice created two versions
from one intent (and fired onEditVersion twice, so the editor jumped), or
sent two renames.

Guard both handlers with refs, which flip synchronously, and reset them in
`finally` so a failed attempt can still be retried.

the new tests now cover blank creation, naming/trimming, Enter/Escape,
onBeforeCreate ordering and failure, rename, delete + confirmation, every
API error path, activeVersionId highlighting, list states, and
formatVersionLabel's edge cases.

subject: fix(admin): stop the preview disconnecting itself mid-connect (#661)
title: stop the preview disconnecting itself mid-connect (#661)
body:
The admin dashboard's roleplay preview sat on "Connecting to session…"
forever. Production logs show the shape exactly: for every preview room the
agent joined within ~5s and published a track, no human participant ever
joined, and the worker gave up at 30s with "No human participant joined
within 30s — orphaned agent". Learner sessions in the same minutes were fine,
which is why this was admin-only — this hook is admin-only.

Two effects in useLiveKitRoom were keyed on callback identity while their
teardown calls `room.disconnect()`:

  - the connect effect depended on [id, cleanupRoom, connectToRoom].
    `connectToRoom` lists `isConnecting`/`isConnected`, which it sets itself on
    the line before it awaits `room.connect()`, and `cleanupRoom` reaches
    `handleDisconnect`, which the page passed as an inline arrow. So it re-ran
    on almost every render and aborted its own in-flight connect.
  - a second, redundant unmount-cleanup effect keyed on [cleanupRoom] did the
    same thing. It is deleted rather than repaired: it only ever guarded
    unmount, which the connect effect's own cleanup already covers.

The connect effect now holds both callbacks in refs and depends on [id], so it
is scoped to the ROOM rather than to render identity, and the timeout still
calls the freshest closure. `handleRoomDisconnected` becomes a useCallback so
the room's Disconnected listener stops churning every render.

Refs rather than a hand-trimmed dependency array, deliberately. This regressed
in a6969afc ("address exhaustive-deps lint warnings"), so dropping a dep would
buy nothing past the next sweep. Refs are stable, so eslint is satisfied by
[id] and the lint rule now agrees with the intended lifetime instead of
fighting it.

Tests pin the invariant rather than the implementation, because the failure is
silent from the outside — no error, no rejected promise, just a page that never
finishes connecting. The re-render case failed with disconnect "called 5 times"
against the first fix alone, which is how the second effect was found.

subject: fix(builder): the budget banner's Raise button crashed the panel
title: the budget banner's Raise button crashed the panel
body:
Carbon forbids interactive children in an InlineNotification and throws when it
finds one: a notification is announced to a screen reader as a single block of
text, so a control buried inside it is unreachable. The budget banner had a
<Button> as a child, so rendering it took out the whole panel and left an error
boundary where the Raise control should have been — on the one session that
needed raising.

ActionableNotification is the component Carbon provides for this. It takes the
button as a prop, so the violation is not expressible.

The markup was not new. It had been there for every live session with a budget
hold; that is rare enough that nobody reached it, and the previous change made
the banner render on stopped sessions, which is where it finally fired.

The reason it shipped is the more useful half. These tests mock the whole design
system, so the component that throws never ran — every test passed while the
live page broke. The mock now mirrors the real constraint: it rejects
interactive children, matching Carbon's actual rule rather than a stricter one,
because a plain <ul> of hints is a legitimate child and StartBuildDialog uses it.

Getting that guard right took two attempts. The first version checked tag names,
which sails straight past a <Button> whose type is a function — exactly the
shape of the real bug. Verified by reintroducing the original markup: the suite
now fails, and passes again when restored.

subject: fix(builder): let a session over its ceiling be raised
title: let a session over its ceiling be raised
body:
The raise control only rendered while the session was live or waiting. For a
hold that is right — a hold is a run counting down on the ceiling, and it goes
stale the moment the run ends. For `exceeded` it is exactly backwards: the
ceiling is *why* the session stopped, so hiding the control on a stopped session
hid the only way to restart it.

A real session is in that state now. It stopped over budget with a question
still unanswered, and the unanswered question parks its run in
WAITING_FOR_INPUT, which counts as an active run, which makes every review and
fix dispatch return null. The budget is the first domino and the raise is the
only way to reach it — but the session reads FAILED, so the banner never
rendered: no spend, no explanation, no button. Every route out of the session
was behind the thing doing the blocking.

`raiseBudget` has no status guard on the server, which is the same judgement
made in the same place: a ceiling is meant to be raisable from wherever the
session stopped. Only the UI disagreed.

Still hidden once a raise could not change anything — a completed or cancelled
session's ceiling is history.

subject: fix(builder): stop losing the reason a build wouldn't start
title: stop losing the reason a build wouldn't start
body:
"Couldn't start a new build." was the only thing the UI said when the server had
told it exactly what was wrong. It happened twice, to two different people, for
the same reason both times: the hero box is a four-line textarea asking what you
want built, so people type a paragraph — and the whole paragraph was sent as
`title`, which the server caps at 200 characters.

Capping the input would have been the wrong fix. It would truncate what you are
telling the agent, and the typed text is not really a title — it is the opening
message the interview reacts to. So the title is now derived from it and the
full text still travels as the opening turn. The title only seeds the branch
slug, and the agent rewrites it once the PRD takes shape.

Derived at a word boundary where there is one in the last quarter, because
"…for individual liste" reads like a bug and "…for individual" reads like a
title; a single enormous token has no boundary to honour and is simply cut.

Failures now show what the server said. class-validator returns an array of
field errors and Nest returns a string; both beat the generic line, which is
kept for errors carrying nothing to show — a network drop, or a 500.

The helpers live in their own module rather than the page: importing the page
into a test pulls in Redux at module load, which is the trap CLAUDE.md warns
about and which cost a red suite before I moved them.

Verified by mutation: removing the truncation turns 3 of the 8 new tests red.
317 files / 5294 tests green.

subject: fix(tracks): renumber article question chips when an earlier one is deleted
title: renumber article question chips when an earlier one is deleted
body:
Found by driving the node in a real browser: delete the first question and
the one after it went on calling itself "Question 2", so it no longer matched
the question fields below the editor — which are numbered by document
position for exactly the purpose of matching.

A chip's number depends on what is before it, and ProseMirror never calls a
node view's `update` for a change outside its own node, so the surviving view
was never told anything had happened. The view now recomputes its label on
every transaction and detaches the listener when it is destroyed.

Regression covered with the node mounted, which is what makes the node view
run at all — the earlier suite exercised the schema only.

subject: fix(helpline): send simulation-credits userId as a query param
title: send simulation-credits userId as a query param
body:
The previous commit appended the userId as a path segment
(/v1/simulation-credits/7), but the backend route is a plain
`@Get()` on `v1/simulation-credits` that reads `userId` from
`@Query()` — so the path-segment form matches no route at all
and 404s. Send it as a query param instead, and omit it entirely
when the id isn't available yet so the token-derived fallback
still works for ordinary learners.

Replaces the regression test, which imported `msw` and
`@mocks/server` — neither exists in this repo, so the Vitest job
failed to resolve the module. The new test pins the request
descriptor (url + params) instead, which is what actually
regressed.

subject: fix(scribe): stop a failed refetch from wiping logs and summaries
title: stop a failed refetch from wiping logs and summaries
body:
Sushil (09-09) and Dhanashree (09-10) both hit a full-page "Unable to
load call logs" / "Summary Not Found" on data they had just been
reading. Nothing was wrong server-side: over those 48h the only
failures prod recorded on /v1/chats/* were 401s on a near-exact
15-minute cadence — routine access-token expiry, which the app absorbs
by refreshing and retrying (2 refresh failures in 20h). One transient
rejection was enough to wall them out until a hard reload.

RTK Query's isLoading is true only for a cache entry's FIRST load. A
rejected *background* refetch leaves isError true, isLoading false and
the last good data still cached — so `isError && !isLoading` fires with
rows sitting in the store, and the tables threw them away. Both tables
set refetchOnFocus, so a refetch runs every time the counsellor tabs
back into the browser: precisely when a 15-minute-old token has most
likely just expired. CallSummary has the same shape, and is hit harder
because every autosave invalidates the CallSummary tag and refetches.

Show the error state only when there is genuinely nothing to render:
no accumulated rows, or no cached summary. The existing toast already
tells the counsellor a refresh failed, which is the right weight for
something that fixes itself on the next poll.

Not a new regression — the tables' fallback came in with 7c4b8d7f
(2026-08-24) and CallSummary's with ce255b01. It needs a refetch to be
rejected to show, which is why it surfaces as one user on one day
rather than everyone at once.

subject: fix: getActiveTooltips error loop worse than filed: worst session hit endpoint 66 times in 5 min (#623)
title: getActiveTooltips error loop worse than filed: worst session hit endpoint 66 times in 5 min (#623)
body:
Telemetry from 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-06 showed 9 sessions and 6 users still
error-looping on getActiveTooltips after the prior fix (#580), with the
worst session hitting it 66 times in under 5 minutes — 13x the "up to 5
times" the prior fix was scoped against.

#580 bounded AppTooltip's refetchOnMountOrArgChange to 30s, but RTK Query
only honours that window once a query has fulfilled at least once: with no
fulfilledTimeStamp to compare against, its mount-time condition() check
(isForcedQuery) forces a fresh request on every new subscription regardless
of the window. AppTooltip wraps controls on nearly every routed page, so
while the endpoint is persistently failing, every single remount re-hit it
with no backoff at all — exactly the scenario the telemetry caught, and the
one case the prior bound didn't cover.

Track the last failure across mounts (the query takes no argument, so every
AppTooltip instance shares one cache entry) and skip re-subscribing until a
30s cooldown passes, regardless of RTK Query's own fulfilled-timestamp
tracking.

Regression test: AppTooltip.errorLoop.test.tsx mounts/unmounts AppTooltip
five times against a real RTK Query api that always errors — it fails
against the old code (5 attempts, one per mount) and passes now (throttled
to 1).

subject: fix(video-actor): keep covers manual for a face with no picture
title: keep covers manual for a face with no picture
body:
Selecting a Beyond Presence face cleared the author's cover video and supplied
no cover image in its place, leaving them strictly worse off than before they
picked a face: no video, no replacement, and an image the avatar never provided.

The clear was unconditional, but its justification is not. Clearing exists for
consistency — once the cover image becomes this face, a previously uploaded
video of somebody else is a visible mismatch, and we cannot import the face's
own clip. That reasoning only holds when the face actually supplies the image.

Beyond Presence publishes no thumbnails at all (its OpenAPI spec has no
thumbnail/preview/image_url field anywhere), so such a face supplies nothing,
the cover image stays the author's own, and their video is still consistent with
it. Those roleplays now keep both covers fully manual, and the notice says so
rather than reporting a removal.

subject: fix(video-actor): clear fields with null, so removing a face actually saves
title: clear fields with null, so removing a face actually saves
body:
Reported: remove the avatar, choose a cover photo instead, and the change does
not autosave.

Cause is a trap this codebase has hit before. Clearing a field to `undefined`
looks right in the form, but JSON.stringify DROPS undefined keys — so the
autosave payload omits the field entirely, the backend never learns it was
cleared, and the old face survives. From the author's side that is
indistinguishable from "the save didn't happen". Exactly the scribe
custom-fields bug, where the fix was likewise to send null.

Every clear path now sends null: the face and provider in clearFace, the cover
video cleared on selection (which had the same defect and would also have
failed to persist), the cover image when a vendor publishes no still, and the
manual id box when emptied. `@IsOptional()` on ally-be's DTO accepts null, and
scenario.util passes it straight through to metadata as a real cleared value.

Clearing the FACE still leaves the covers alone: blanking a roleplay's cover
image because an avatar was deselected would be its own bug.

Also fixed the test stub that made this class of bug invisible: getValues()
ignored its argument and returned the whole values object — always truthy — so
every "did this field have a value?" check passed regardless.

110 tests in create-simulation-sub-section, tsc clean.

subject: fix(video-actor): clear the cover video when a face is selected
title: clear the cover video when a face is selected
body:
Reported by an author: upload a cover image AND a cover video, then pick a
face. The cover image became that face, while the cover video stayed as the
person they had uploaded — so the roleplay showed one person's photograph
beside a different person's video.

The previous commit left cover video untouched on purpose, reasoning that a
video present is the author's own upload and overwriting it destroys their
work. That reasoning was wrong about which outcome is worse. We cannot import
the face's own clip — the vendors' run to 54 MB against the 15 MB the uploader
allows — so the choice is between no video and a mismatched one, and empty is
the honest state.

Cleared in onFaceSelect rather than inside applyFaceCover, so it happens even
when the face publishes no picture or the import fails: the mismatch is just as
wrong in those cases. Only dirtied when there was actually a video, and the
notice now says "Cover video was cleared to match" so a removal the author did
not ask for is never silent. Clearing the FACE leaves the covers alone —
blanking a roleplay's cover because an avatar was deselected would be its own
version of this bug.

Also fixes the test stub that hid this class of bug: getValues() ignored its
argument and returned the whole values object, which is truthy, so every
"did this field have a value?" assertion silently passed.

110 tests in create-simulation-sub-section, tsc clean.

subject: fix(admin): stop an unset table cell from crashing the page
title: stop an unset table cell from crashing the page
body:
A NotionTable cell is handed either the {value, disabled, rowId} wrapper the
pages build or a bare value, and Cell told them apart by whether `value` was
defined. An unset field — an event with no occurrence interval, an empty score —
therefore read as a bare value, so the wrapper object itself flowed into the
read-only branches that print their value. React threw "Objects are not valid as
a React child (found: object with keys {value, disabled, rowId})" and the error
boundary replaced the whole Events page.

Detect the wrapper by shape instead, so an explicitly-undefined value unwraps to
undefined and the read-only branches render their "--" placeholder. This covers
the disabled dropdown branch too, which had the same leak.

subject: fix(admin/bug-hunter): re-enable Scan now button when a watched scan stalls
title: re-enable Scan now button when a watched scan stalls
body:
When the actively-watched UX Signals scan crosses the staleness cutoff
while the panel is still mounted, the watch effect stopped polling but
never cleared watchedScanId. The finalize effect never clears it either,
since it bails out whenever lastScan.status === RUNNING, which a stalled
row never leaves. isBusy still included Boolean(watchedScanId)
unconditionally, so the "Scan now" button stayed disabled forever even
though the panel correctly told the admin the scan had stalled and a new
one could be started. The only workaround was reloading the page.

Fix: clear watchedScanId in the watch effect when a previously-running
scan transitions to stalled.

goes stale mid-wait" in UxSignalsPanel.test.tsx exercises a scan that
starts running (button disabled from the click) and then goes stale
while still mounted - the actual failure path, distinct from the
existing "stale at mount" test.

title: stop premature getCallLogs/getCallTags 401s and empty-name updateCallInfo 400s (#585)

corrected it to ORG_LOGS in a useEffect. Users who hold only

subject: fix(track-player): wire completed segments in the progress rail to jump navigation (#584)
title: wire completed segments in the progress rail to jump navigation (#584)
body:
Dead-click telemetry showed unlabelled-control clicks clustering on both
/track/.../item/... routes (10 and 14 clicks across sessions, threshold 5).
The segmented progress rail in PlayerTopBar renders one colored, hover-free
span per item in the section — visually a step indicator, but wired with no
onClick at all, so every tap on it was a genuine dead click. The navigation
hook already exposed a `goToItem(itemId)` helper for exactly this purpose,
but nothing ever called it.

Completed segments now render as buttons that call `goToItem` to let a
learner revisit finished content; in-progress/locked segments stay inert
spans so the existing next-item completion gating isn't bypassed.

segment invokes the jump handler and an unlocked segment isn't exposed as
a clickable control (was failing before the fix — no accessible button was
rendered).
