subject: feat(voices): label a saved voice's picker on open, and let the v3 advisory expire
title: label a saved voice's picker on open, and let the v3 advisory expire
body:
A production voice showed its v3 warning correctly — the bulk sync had filled in
`voice_type` — while its model picker sat unlabelled, because the per-voice
recommendation comes from ElevenLabs' fine-tune list and is never stored. The
only way to see it was to press "Re-check" on that one voice. The panel now
sends a saved ElevenLabs voice's id with its catalog request, so ally-be returns
the verdict with the options and the labels are there on open.

Only for a saved voice: while a new voice's id is still being typed, an
id-shaped-but-wrong value would only produce failed lookups, and the debounced
lookup already covers that case with results that take precedence anyway.

The amber v3 advisory now defers to the same verdict. It read voice type alone,
so when ElevenLabs ship the support their wording already anticipates — v3
"doesn't YET support Professional Voice Clones" — it would have kept insisting
the training cannot be used. The verdict may only silence it, never raise it, so
each message still chooses its own wording, and with no verdict at all the
voice-type rule stands: losing the advisory for lack of data would be the worst
of the three outcomes, since silence is what let 23 production rows end up
misconfigured.

Both surfaces now read one verdict, so the picker label and the banner cannot
contradict each other.

subject: feat(voices): narrow a voice picker to the gender being configured
title: narrow a voice picker to the gender being configured
body:
A Tamil Google voice offered 68 options with roughly half the wrong gender.
ally-be now publishes each catalog entry's gender, so the picker shows only the
voices that match — reading the field rather than parsing it back out of the
display label.

Only a gender we actually model may exclude a voice. Everything else counts as
unknown and is kept:

- absent, empty, or whitespace — all 102 Deepgram models and 1 Hume voice
  report no gender at all, so treating absence as a mismatch would empty
  Deepgram's picker entirely
- a category we don't model — Google's NEUTRAL today, whatever a provider adds
  next; a new value upstream must never silently hide voices
- the value already saved on this voice, so changing gender cannot quietly
  rewrite the voice a scenario actually uses

Compared trimmed and lower-cased on both sides, because stored genders are not
reliably normalised — ally-be's own voice lookup compares
`LOWER(config ->> 'gender')` for that reason. And if a gender ends up with no
voices of its own the full list comes back, since an empty picker reads as
"this provider has no voices".

description: narrow a voice picker to the gender being configured

subject: feat(admin): test a Language Model config against its provider
title: test a Language Model config against its provider
body:
ADR Phase 4a, client half. A "Test model" button in the Language Model
side panel calls the new preview endpoint and shows the reply, latency and
token usage — or the provider's own error.

Lives in the side panel rather than a table column for three reasons: the
result needs room (a deprecation notice names the replacement model, and a
cell would truncate exactly the useful part), it sits beside the model
field you would edit to fix it, and it avoids adding a cell type to the
shared NotionTable, whose blast radius covers every table in the product.

onTest is optional, so Speech Recognition does not grow a button it cannot
use — testing STT needs audio input, not a text prompt. The control only
appears for a saved row, since the check runs against what is stored
rather than what is currently typed.

ok:false arrives as a 200 and is rendered as a result, not swallowed as an
error; only a genuinely failed request falls into the catch. The provider's
message is shown verbatim in a wrapping block.

The stored result is cleared when another config is opened — otherwise a
stale outcome reads as if it described the newly opened row. That one is
mutation-checked: removing the reset fails its test.

Improve the cross-app shared component library (consumed by all three apps)
without changing any public component API:

Toggle

Dropdown / DropdownField

  onClose prop

Badge

ButtonGroup spec. Full ui-shared suite passes (241 tests); typecheck and lint
clean.

Note: broad semantic color tokenization was deliberately deferred. A parity
check found ally-web defines no color palette and the helpline/admin palettes
diverge, so mapping shared neutrals to tokens would shift rendered colors

title: scope to email allowlist (drop env flag)
body:
Replace the `SELECTABLE_MAIN_AGENT_PROMPT_FLAG` env flag with a small
email-based allowlist hook. The env-var injection path didn't survive the
baremetal/TeamCity build pipeline reliably, and per-user permission gating
isn't wired up yet — so an in-code allowlist lets the two test accounts
exercise the feature in any deployed environment without infra changes.

New hook (`hooks/useCanUseSelectablePrompts.ts`):
- Hardcoded allowlist of 4 emails (two human testers + their +admin
  variants).
- Reads the logged-in user's email from Redux (`state.user.user.email`)
  and returns whether they're cleared to use the feature.

Gating sites — all replaced flag check with the hook:
- `useIsPlaceholderUsed` — when the user isn't on the allowlist the
  hook short-circuits to `kind: "no_selection"` regardless of stored
  `selectedMainPromptCode`. Body-driven gates fall back to the legacy
  Prompt #1 view, non-destructive (DB variant code preserved).
- `PromptSidePanel` — "Duplicate as variant" and "Delete variant"
  buttons hidden for non-allowlist users.
- `CreateSimulationSubSection` — drops the `selectedMainPromptCode`
  picker field from the rendered items list for non-allowlist users,
  avoiding the empty `w-full` wrapper that self-hiding alone would
  leave behind.
- `SimulationCreator.ts` — picker field always declared; runtime
  filtering moves to the layout layer (no more static
  `FEATURE_FLAGS_MAP ? […] : []` shape).
- `featureFlag.ts` — `SELECTABLE_MAIN_AGENT_PROMPT_FLAG` entry removed.

Tests updated:
- `PromptSidePanel.test.tsx` and `CreateSimulationSubSection.test.tsx`:
  mock `@hooks` so `useCanUseSelectablePrompts` returns true without a
  Redux provider.
- `FormField.test.tsx`: mock `@hooks` to stub `useIsPlaceholderUsed`
  directly (FormField uses it transitively; the real hook now pulls
  `useSelector`).

When ready to GA: replace the allowlist body with `return true` or

subject: feat(prompt-variants): hide entry points behind feature flag
title: hide entry points behind feature flag
body:
Gate the selectable-main-agent-variants entry points behind a new env
flag (`VITE_SELECTABLE_MAIN_AGENT_PROMPT_FLAG`) so the feature can ship
to prod dark while it's still being validated in dev. Per-user
permission gating will replace this env flag in a follow-up.

What the flag hides when off:
- Main-agent prompt picker field in edit-simulation (SimulationCreator).
  Scenarios stay on the default Prompt #1; `selectedMainPromptCode`
  isn't writable through the UI.
- "Duplicate as variant" + "Delete variant" buttons in PromptSidePanel.
  Admins can still edit existing prompts (branching, evaluator, blocks,
  Prompt #1 body, etc.) but can't create or remove `_copy_*` variant
  rows — keeps the rest of Prompt Management usable.

What the flag DOESN'T hide:
- Prompt Management page itself — it predates variants and is used to
  manage non-variant prompts too.
- The Behaviour Instructions table — it always renders for scoring.

Hook short-circuit (`useIsPlaceholderUsed`):
- When the flag is off, the hook returns `kind: "no_selection"`
  regardless of any stored `selectedMainPromptCode` on the scenario.
- Routes every body-driven gate into its legacy fallback path:
  StatesEditor self-hides, BehavioursAndStatesInstruction shows all
  per-state coaching columns, FormField shows all annotated fields.
- Non-destructive: the DB row's variant code is preserved; flipping the
  flag back on restores the variant view exactly.

BehavioursAndStatesInstruction `no_selection` fallback:
- When no variant is selected (flag off, or scenario predates picker),
  the runtime resolves to default Prompt #1 — which has
  `{behavior_instructions_json}` and no `{state_x_guidelines}`. The UI
  gate now mirrors that fallback so legacy scenarios keep their
  per-state coaching columns visible instead of disappearing into a
  "no_selection" edge case.

Prod safety: even with the flag on at the env level, the studio's
runtime UI and ally-ai-learn's runtime resolver agree for every
scenario configuration that exists today.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: hide entry points behind feature flag

was TEXT. That made AI fill discoverable only after committing to a
type, and a direct API call could still combine AI with non-TEXT.

Step 1 now asks the user to pick fill mode (Manual or AI fill) up
front. The field-type list below filters accordingly: all enabled
types when Manual, TEXT only when AI. Switching to AI auto-selects
TEXT; switching back to Manual clears any in-progress AI instruction
and restores the first enabled type.

Step 2 drops the redundant AI-fill toggle in the create flow (it's
locked in by step 1) but keeps it in the edit flow so existing
fields' fill mode stays toggleable. The AI instruction textarea
still appears whenever selectedType === TEXT && fillMode === AI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: ask fill mode before field type when creating a custom field

subject: feat(debrief): let the supervisor note reference its own live notes
title: let the supervisor note reference its own live notes
body:
The live-supervisor feature sends a learner short coaching hints during a
roleplay. This threads those hints into the debrief evaluation as `live_notes`
so the closing note can pick one of them up — "I nudged you about slowing
down; you did, and you can hear the difference" — instead of delivering the
same point cold to someone who already read it.

Also amends an honesty rule that the feature had quietly outdated. The prompt
forbade claiming to have "listened live"; where live notes exist the
supervisor really was reading along as it happened, so "I saw" and "I flagged
at the time" are now allowed while "I heard" still is not.

The empty case is stated as a fact ("You gave no live notes during this
session.") rather than left blank, because a blank there makes the model
invent advice it never gave.

Verified: 117 tests across text_generations + summaries, including new cases
for the empty, whitespace-only and populated branches.

subject: feat(transcript): mark which kind of client utterance a line is
title: mark which kind of client utterance a line is
body:
A thinking filler, an interim reply and the real reply all reach Core as CLIENT
lines, and one turn can emit all three in a row. Nothing distinguished them, so
a consumer had to infer kind from position — and position is ambiguous the
moment a continuation filler plays, which makes two fillers precede the reply.

Adds ChatMessage.utterance_kind ('reply' | 'filler' | 'interim'), set at each of
the three emitters. Values match the metadata.firstAudioSource vocabulary
already on the turn-metrics row, so the transcript and the latency record join
cleanly rather than needing a second mapping.

None means an older worker and is deliberately distinct from 'reply': reading
that silence as a real reply would mislabel every filler already in the backlog.

This unblocks the ally-be half of the filler evaluation, which has to pair each
played filler with the learner turn it answered and the reply that followed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DBRVAhV1dsnm7RupuhBtu7
description: mark which kind of client utterance a line is

subject: feat(working-memory): the stance selects the authored state guidance
title: the stance selects the authored state guidance
body:
The synthesis Ankita asked for, minus the part that would have been a mistake.

Authors already write state guidance as client POSTURE. Scenario 440's four
bands read "Dis-engaged, feeling discouraged and confused", "Feels heard and is
open to sharing", "Explores fears and preferences", "Confident to draw boundary
assertively". That is a stance ladder. The score was only the index into it —
and a lossy one, since two very different sessions reach the same number.

Worse, in production it barely moves. State resolution reads ScoreKeeper's
EVENT bucket, while the behaviours authors actually write under "Helper should
do" land in the BEHAVIOUR bucket: 15 positively-scored behaviour items over 12h
fleet-wide produced exactly one change in the score states are selected by, and
it was -5. So the authored guidance sat still for a whole session and it looked
like the states had stopped working.

Selecting by stance indexes the same guidance with something that had to be
EARNED: one rung per turn, a two-turn dwell, an immediate drop on rupture, and
now — via 642ec6f — advanceable by the behaviour scores the author configured.

ORDINAL mapping, not by name. Authors did not label bands with stance names and
are not being asked to. States arrive pre-sorted by scoreLower, so their order
already encodes the intended progression; the ladder's order encodes ours;
position maps to position. No new field, no migration, no per-scenario config —
which is what makes this shippable without touching the library. A scenario
with more than five bands compresses and some become unreachable: a real cost,
stated rather than hidden, and the price of not demanding a re-authoring pass.

NOT a migration. Scoped to prompts that opted into working memory and only when
a stance exists to map; unknown or absent stances fall back to score-based
selection rather than to nothing. Every other scenario resolves exactly as it
does today, and the rollback is the one the design already documents:
re-select a different prompt.

What deliberately did NOT change: the score still drives learner feedback, the
report and evaluation. Ankita's instinct was to replace the score mechanism
entirely; that would also have handed control of what counts from the author to
the updater LLM, which is less authorial control, not more. Replacing the
COUPLING keeps both.

Logs the disagreement at INFO whenever stance and score would have chosen
differently, so the two indexes can be compared on real sessions before anyone
argues for going further.

1722 unit tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: the stance selects the authored state guidance

subject: feat(working-memory): fall back to what the session is ABOUT when the conversation offers no cue
title: fall back to what the session is ABOUT when the conversation offers no cue
body:
Recall had two cue tiers — topics the updater nominated, then the learner's own
words. When both are empty it scored by encoding strength and decay alone,
which picks five true facts about the client but not the five this conversation
is about. The failure mode is blandness, not error, so nothing surfaces it.

Two situations reach that state and neither is exotic:

- The OPENING turn. `recall.select` runs inside consolidation, which runs after
  a learner turn, so on the agent's first utterance `salient_backstory` is
  simply empty and the block renders "(nothing from your own life is on your
  mind this turn)". The client has identity — role_instructions, name, age,
  profession, state guidance are separate placeholders — but no episodic
  detail at the moment it introduces itself.
- Any content-free learner turn. "mm-hmm", "okay", "go on" yield no usable
  keywords, and the document-frequency filter discards whatever generic tokens
  survive.

Tier 3 is the scenario DESCRIPTION. Deliberately not the opening statement:
openings are written to be generic ("they told me I have to come here"), while
the description says what the session is actually about — scenario 424's reads
"his scores have dropped sharply... something happened at his home recently" —
which is what should pull the grief facts forward on turn one rather than
leaving the choice to decay ordering. It is the same field the branching prompt
already renders as {challenge_description}.

Strictly a last resort: the tests pin that a real learner utterance still
outranks it, or recall would stop responding to what is being said.

Measured cost of NOT doing this was zero — Preparation scored 78.8 in both arms
across 8 prod runs — so this is a small sharpening, not a fix for a defect.

19 recall tests, 284 across working memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: fall back to what the session is ABOUT when the conversation offers no cue

subject: feat(working-memory): say whether the feature engaged, and why not
title: say whether the feature engaged, and why not
body:
One INFO line per session naming the opt-in decision and its reason.

The off state has been indistinguishable from the on state from outside the
process. A session that has not opted in produces a full transcript, a good
score and no errors — it simply lacks the block. That is precisely how a prod
run went 8/8 exchanges looking perfect while the feature was silently disabled:
the prompt was file-backed, so ally-be never dispatched it
(getPromptsForScenarioSession filters useDashboardOverrideOnly) and the
placeholder check found nothing to opt in on. Finding that took correlating
[PROMPT_SOURCE] lines in CloudWatch, because the only existing signal for the
off path was logger.debug and prod runs at INFO.

Anyone authoring a scenario against this feature has to be able to answer "did
it engage?" without that. The not-engaged branch names which of the three gates
failed, and points at the useDashboardOverride trap by name, since that is the
one with no other symptom.

    [working-memory] ENGAGED room=ss_... — scenario opted in via the
    {client_working_memory} placeholder

    [working-memory] NOT ENGAGED room=ss_... — the selected main-agent prompt
    does not declare {client_working_memory} — if it should, check the prompt
    has useDashboardOverride=true, or ally-be will not ship it to the worker

Shipping now because the team is about to author scenarios against this:
without it they would report "feels about the same" with no way to know whether
the feature was on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: say whether the feature engaged, and why not

subject: feat(session): tag the emergency-finalize end-of-session message with a reason
title: tag the emergency-finalize end-of-session message with a reason
body:
The stall watchdog's force-exit path (EmergencyFinalizer) already carries
an internal `reason` string (e.g. "watchdog_force_exit") for logging, but
the end-of-session SQS message it sends was byte-identical to a clean
finish's, so ally-be had no way to tell a technically-interrupted session
apart from a normal one.

Threads that existing reason through create_session_end_message as a new,
additive `reason` field on the message's event_data. Omitted entirely on
the normal finalize_session path, so those messages are unchanged.
event_data is a loose, unvalidated dict on both ends of this pipe (no
pydantic model, no DTO/class-validator on ally-be's consumer), so this is
a safe additive change with no schema migration on either side.

Pairs with an ally-be change (persists the reason as a new endReason
column) and an ally-web change (shows the learner a clear message instead
of the normal debrief screen when this fires).

Verified: both edited files parse cleanly (ast.parse). Could not run the
repo's pytest/ruff suite in this environment (no poetry/venv available) -
worth running `make test` before merging.

subject: feat(working-memory): wire the store into the worker and run config
title: wire the store into the worker and run config
body:
Phase 2 complete. Still behaviour-neutral: the store is constructed and
reachable, and nothing reads it.

Worker-owned beside RollingSummaryStore and RetrievedContextStore, for the reason
§5 gives: agent_graph is compiled once at import and shared by every concurrent
session in the process, so the per-session run config is the only place
per-session identity exists. Passed through create_agent_with_adapter into
`configurable`, which is also what lets a future graph node no-op cleanly when it
is absent — how the report graph degrades, having no worker and therefore no
store.

DELIBERATELY NOT CALLING begin_turn() YET, and the reason is worth recording
because the obvious placement is wrong. It has to advance the turn counter
BEFORE the reply is generated, or the prompt that reads the memory and the update
that later writes it disagree about which turn they are discussing — and the
monotonic check then has nothing meaningful to compare. The tempting hook is
handlers.py's speech-end branch, next to turn_metrics.note_user_speech_end, but
that handler is synchronous and begin_turn is not: scheduling it as a task means
it may land after generation has already started. So it belongs in the graph,
alongside the updater, which is phase 3. Until then the counter sits at 0 on
every session and nothing depends on it.

Teardown added now rather than left for phase 3 to remember. The record needs
none — it is an instance attribute that dies with the worker, unlike
turn_metrics' module-level dicts keyed by room — but a detached update still
running at session end would write into a store nobody will read and hold a
reference to the LLM client past teardown. `discard()` is synchronous so it sits
in the shutdown path beside the other cleanups, and it cancels the task WITHOUT
clearing state: a shutdown racing finalize must not lose the session's memory
before it can be written out.

Three tests on teardown, including that discard is a no-op when nothing is
running — shutdown runs on every session, including ones where no update ever
started. 1,541 tests pass across tests/unit and tests/roleplay_v2, the latter
included deliberately: phase 2 lifted code out of that package's neighbourhood
and its 143 tests are the check that nothing moved underneath it.

Docs-Skip: docs/client-working-memory-design.md specifies this and is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: wire the store into the worker and run config

subject: feat(transcript): carry whether the learner talked over a client turn
title: carry whether the learner talked over a client turn
body:
LiveKit builds the assistant ChatMessage it emits as:

    msg = self._agent._chat_ctx.add_message(
        role="assistant",
        content=forwarded_text,
        interrupted=speech_handle.interrupted,
        ...)

Two things follow, and the second is the reason for this change. `content` is
`forwarded_text` — the part of the reply that reached TTS before the utterance
stopped — so on an interrupted turn the transcript holds a PREFIX of what the
model produced, not the whole thing. And `interrupted` is right there on the
message, per utterance, and we were throwing it away.

Measured across judged turns: a cut turn keeps ~36% of the generated characters
(54 of 194 on average) against ~107% on an uncut one, and 27.8% of ALL judged
turns kept under 70%. That prefix is why `truncation` is the second-largest
language-judge annotation category at 1,109 — the judge was reading a cut-off
sentence as the actor failing to finish one. It also distorts the rest: fragments
DILUTE persona_break, because a 54-character prefix gives a judge less material
in which to find the client acting like an assistant.

The flag now rides on the transcript ChatMessage to Core (ally-be 023f13bf
persists it and hands it to the judge, which conditions `truncation` on it —
ally-ai fc88d6d).

None is not False. A COUNSELOR turn has no such notion and an older LiveKit build
has no such attribute, and neither may be read as "known not to be interrupted"
— the judge conditions on presence, so a spurious false would condition out a
real defect. Read with getattr so a missing attribute can never stop a transcript
publishing: losing the flag is a nuisance, losing the turn is data loss.

Five tests, including the counsellor-turn and missing-attribute cases. 1,312
unit tests pass.

an optional field to an existing transcript message rather than an event type.

description: carry whether the learner talked over a client turn

subject: feat(turn-detection): per-scenario override for max endpointing delay
title: per-scenario override for max endpointing delay
body:
TURN_MAX_ENDPOINTING_DELAY was a single platform-wide ceiling on how long
semantic turn-detection waits for a learner who seems mid-thought before
replying anyway. Adds prompt_data.turn_max_endpointing_delay so an individual
scenario can pick its own speed-vs-interruption trade-off instead of sharing
one global value, gated by TURN_ENDPOINTING_SCENARIO_OVERRIDE_ENABLED (a
global kill-switch defaulting True) so it can be disabled instantly without
a redeploy. Defaults to unset (None) for every scenario, so no behavior
changes until a scenario explicitly sets it. worker_v2 (roleplay_v2, a
different Persona/spec model with no equivalent field) intentionally keeps
using the global setting only.

The episodic-memory rollout is validated (live A/B runs + ten automated
v2v sessions: latency-neutral at p50, ~$0.001/session summarizer cost,
memory rows and structured disclosures verified end to end), so the

subject: feat(filler): randomized delay + probability so fillers feel natural
title: randomized delay + probability so fillers feel natural
body:
Fillers fired on every thinking transition, which felt unnatural. Make
them need-based and occasional:
- wait a random delay in [FILLER_MIN_DELAY_MS, FILLER_MAX_DELAY_MS]
  (300-600ms) after the learner stops;
- skip entirely if the reply is ready by then (no gap to mask);
- even when there is a gap, play only FILLER_PLAY_PROBABILITY (0.6) of the
  time so the agent doesn't fill on every pause.
description: randomized delay + probability so fillers feel natural

subject: feat(latency): default BEHAVIORS_OFF_GATE=True (de-gate behavior scoring)
title: default BEHAVIORS_OFF_GATE=True (de-gate behavior scoring)
body:
Run detect_behaviors in parallel with the reply instead of gating it, removing
~1.3s from the voice-to-voice critical path. Behaviors only drive scoring + UI
feedback; branching that shapes the reply travels as events through
process_events, whose edge to the sync node is unconditional, so it still gates
the response regardless of this flag — de-gating behaviors never drops branching.
Scores/feedback still accumulate every turn. Set False to restore gating.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: default BEHAVIORS_OFF_GATE=True (de-gate behavior scoring)

subject: feat(prompt): strict body-driven state gate + character backstory in Prompt #2
title: strict body-driven state gate + character backstory in Prompt #2
body:
Remove the legacy `hasStates` fallback from `_get_selected_prompt_has_states`.
`availableVariables` is now the single source of truth: the active state's
guidelines are injected into `{state_x_guidelines}` iff the variant's
reconciled list contains that placeholder. Pairs with the backend
BackfillAvailableVariables1780150000000 migration that populates the list
for every existing row, so no row falls through to the deprecated flag.

Add `{character_profile_text}` to `main_agent_prompt_full.txt` (Prompt #2)
so the character's backstory — already collected in the studio — actually
reaches the prompt. Without it, the LLM had no grounding for the
character's history and confabulated details.

Tests updated to assert the new semantics: a prompts entry with
`hasStates=true` but no `state_x_guidelines` in its reconciled list
returns False; empty/missing list returns False as well.

subject: feat(simulation): unify language label with per-scenario override
title: unify language label with per-scenario override
body:
Carry the new `languageCharacteristics` field from backend promptData
through PromptData into the multilingual instructions block, and
unify it with the existing `languageLabel` as a single concept on
the Python side. New `_resolve_effective_language_label` helper picks
the per-scenario override when set, falls back to the DB-derived
label, and finally to the bare locale code — so the LLM gets exactly
one source of truth in the `Output language:` line regardless of
whether the scenario author wrote anything.

Trim the multilingual block to a single template file with one
`{language_label}` slot. The earlier "structural region rule"
paragraph is gone — when authors opt out of writing an override they
still get the DB label, which is a strong-enough signal on its own
once the locale code is also rendered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: unify language label with per-scenario override

subject: feat(simulation): inject regional dialect block for English variants
title: inject regional dialect block for English variants
body:
Region-tagged English locales (en-IN, en-US, en-GB) were short-circuited
out of the multilingual prompt block alongside bare "en", which left the
LLM with no regional signal — all three English variants collapsed to
the model's default English distribution (typically American English).

Tighten the early return so only unspecified language or bare "en" is
skipped. Region-tagged English now flows into the multilingual block
and gets the same dialect-anchored instruction as other languages,
rendering "Output language: English (India) (locale: en-IN)" with the
"region code is mandatory" guidance.

Update the existing English-omission test to cover both behaviours:
region-tagged English includes the dialect block; bare "en" still
omits it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: inject regional dialect block for English variants

subject: feat(simulation): inject language label into multilingual prompt block
title: inject language label into multilingual prompt block
body:
Carry the human-readable language name (e.g. "Tamil (India)") from
backend metadata through PromptData into the multilingual instructions
block, alongside the BCP-47 locale. Strengthens the prompt template
with an explicit, region-anchored dialect rule so models stop falling
back to the training-distribution dialect of the base language.

- PromptData: add `language_label`, mapped from backend `languageLabel`.
- prompt.py: thread label into `_get_language_sample_block`; fall back
  to the code when no label is supplied so older metadata still renders.
- multilingual_instructions_block.txt: render `{language_label} (locale:
  {language_code})` and make the region code mandatory, not advisory.
- Tests: cover label-present, label-absent fallback, and camelCase
  normalization paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
description: inject language label into multilingual prompt block
